nodes.summary: On the index page, moves every 'off'-scored course tile into a per-part, tap-to-expand 'Not shown' box grouped by the reason it was tucked (math comfort / interests / tone), so nothing is deleted — it just recedes into an openable summary.

nodes.name: openOverlay
nodes.summary: Opens the full interest-picker overlay (ensuring it exists), re-renders the topic grid, tone chips, audience selection and undo/redo buttons, locks body scroll, and focuses the first control.

nodes.name: setMathLevel
nodes.summary: Sets the reader's 0-100 math-comfort value (clamped), persisting it and pushing an undo step unless a slider drag batches multiple updates into a single history entry.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Module bootstrap: ensures the 🎯 toggle button and overlay exist, renders the grid, applies visibility (deferring markdown tucking until after renderMarkdown), renders inline widgets, and shows the learned/progress UI.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Core measurement: probes the live weights with a short token window, runs each layer through forwardOneLayer, and per layer computes per-head attention entropy/focus, stable rank of the Q·Kᵀ and V·O blocks, head similarity, dead FFN units, and the residual-stream write magnitudes/cosines, returning a structured report (or null until weights exist).

nodes.name: stableRank
nodes.summary: Computes the stable rank of a matrix as ‖M‖_F² / σ_max(M)² (Frobenius norm squared over the largest singular value, via power iteration), used to report how 'deep' a query-key or value-output circuit is.

nodes.name: attnEntropy
nodes.summary: Computes the mean Shannon entropy (in bits) of a head's causal attention rows, which the concentration metric compares against the causal maximum to gauge how focused each head is.

nodes.name: headSimilarity
nodes.summary: Measures how alike a layer's attention heads are: the mean pairwise Frobenius distance between head weight matrices normalized by the mean head size, where a low value means the heads are near-copies.

nodes.name: describeAttention
nodes.summary: Turns a layer's measured attention metrics into plain-language prose — how sharply focused the heads are, whether heads are near-copies, and what the query-key / value-output effective ranks imply (retrieval vs. multi-directional writes).

nodes.name: describeStream
nodes.summary: Writes the plain-language residual-stream description for a layer: how much of ‖x‖ attention vs. FFN writes, whether the two writes reinforce a shared direction, and whether the layer barely rotates the stream (near-skip).

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the latest measurement into the per-layer cards (preserving which <details> the reader had open), updates the status line, and draws the training sparkline of mean attention-focus and dead-FFN across epochs.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Module entry point: builds the panel chrome (with the bare-equations explainer) and boots the 1.2s measurement tick on DOMContentLoaded (or immediately if already loaded).

nodes.name: safeTextNodes
nodes.summary: Collects the editable text nodes inside a subtree using a TreeWalker, prefiltering to nodes that actually contain fixable characters and rejecting any node whose ancestor is a skipped tag (code/pre/math/etc.), matches a no-typo-fix class, or is contenteditable.

nodes.name: smartQuotes
nodes.summary: Converts straight ' and " in the safe text nodes into curly ‘ ’ “ ” using open/close heuristics (word boundary, apostrophe vs. single quote), returning the number of nodes changed.

nodes.name: smartDashes
nodes.summary: Converts hyphen runs in the safe text nodes into en-dashes (numeric ranges like 1--3) and em-dashes (whitespace-flanked -- and ---), operating on the whole node so GFM table separator rows are left intact.

nodes.name: smartEllipsis
nodes.summary: Replaces an exactly-three-dot run (not part of a longer dot run) with a proper … ellipsis character in the safe text nodes.

nodes.name: fixTypography
nodes.summary: Public API that runs all three autocorrect passes (quotes, dashes, ellipsis) over a root's safe text nodes in a single walk, returning per-category fix counts and the elapsed time.

nodes.name: lint
nodes.summary: Public API that walks the safe text nodes and counts leftover straight quotes / ASCII dashes-in-dash-context / three-dots the autocorrect missed, writing the totals to data-typo-* attributes on <html> and (in debug) to the console.

nodes.name: boot
nodes.summary: One-time bootstrap: runs the first pass after a microtask, re-runs on the blogPostLoadComplete event, starts a debounced MutationObserver on late .md inserts, and exposes window.TypographyFix.

nodes.name: foam_of_meaning.js
nodes.summary: Interactive demos for the 'The foam of meaning' lesson: a self-contained register(fn) component registry that mounts themed Plotly/Canvas/Three.js visualizations for the combinatorial explosion, coherence radar, void classifier, cosmic-web canvas, zoom cascade, phase transition, scaling laws, persistent homology, 3D fiber bundle, commutative square, Tarski truth chain, renormalization group, and a grand synthesis view.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE with a local register/initPhaseSpace registry; every demo guards on its own DOM nodes and initializes on the blogPostLoadComplete event, after renderMarkdown rewrites the .md blocks.

nodes.name: The foam of meaning
nodes.summary: A geometric and topological theory of meaningful language spaces: the possibility space X of linguistic forms, the interpretation map pi:X->S into semantic structures, the world space W, and the landscape of clusters, filaments, and voids, with the renormalization-group and commutativity/compositionality framing.

nodes.name: The Shape of Space — A History of Geometry
nodes.summary: A history of geometry from prehistoric shells and surveying, through Greek proof, Islamic algebra and trigonometry, Renaissance perspective and Descartes' coordinates, to Gauss's Theorema Egregium, non-Euclidean geometry, Riemannian manifolds, and Poincaré's topology, closing on embeddings as the modern need.

nodes.name: The Shape of the Machine — A Working Geometry for AI
nodes.summary: A working geometric toolkit behind neural networks: the inner product and Gram matrix, orthogonal projection, the SVD, steepest-descent, convolution and the DFT, and symmetry (invariance/equivariance), each tied to the layer that uses it, with inline lazy-initialized Plotly interactives.
nodes.languageNotes: Ships its own inline <script> (no separate .js module): a self-booting IIFE that lazily mounts each Plotly plot via IntersectionObserver and re-scales colors through themeColor().

nodes.name: The Shape of Holes: A Working Algebraic Topology
nodes.summary: A working algebraic topology lesson: Euler's bridges, homology chains and the boundary-of-a-boundary rule, homotopy and the fundamental group, exact sequences, Mayer-Vietoris, Seifert-van Kampen, CW complexes, categories, Leray spectral sequences, Steenrod operations, and persistent homology as a bridge to HoTT.

nodes.name: history.js
nodes.summary: Renders the linear-separability demonstration for the Brief History of AI lesson: two Plotly scatter plots showing the OR gate is linearly separable and the XOR gate is not, plus a dark-mode re-render hook.

nodes.name: Brief History of AI
nodes.summary: Traces the convergence of unrelated currents into modern AI: prehistoric counting tools, the Salamis tablet and abacus, number systems, formal logic, computation, and the shifting paths that merged into neural networks and LLMs.

nodes.name: intuition.js
nodes.summary: Interactive visualizations for the LLM intuition lesson covering tokenization, embedding arithmetic, positional encoding, attention, the feed-forward network, the residual stream, final prediction, and the autoregressive loop, using an IntersectionObserver-based lazy-init registry and theme re-rendering.
nodes.languageNotes: Viz components are plain const objects (TokenizerViz, EmbeddingViz, ...) with render methods; loadIntuitionModule registers each section into a lazy init registry driven by IntersectionObserver.

nodes.name: An Intuition of how Large Language Models (LLMs) work
nodes.summary: Explains LLMs as next-word prediction machines and walks the autoregressive loop step by step (user input, appending predicted words until the endoftext token), hosting the interactive visualization containers driven by intuition.js.

nodes.name: language.js
nodes.summary: Builds a vertical interactive timeline of language milestones (from biological capacity for language to LLaMA/ChatGPT) with collapsible deep-dives and click-to-expand descriptions, injecting its CSS via adoptedStyleSheets to avoid reflow.

nodes.name: The History of Language: From Sanskrit to LLMs
nodes.summary: Traces language from the descended larynx and symbolic displacement, through oral mnemonic tradition, clay tokens, writing, and formal grammar (Panini, Frege), to the distributional embeddings and Transformers of modern LLMs.

nodes.name: Basic Math Concepts I — The Numerical Foundations
nodes.summary: The first of three math chapters covering numerical foundations for AI: programming and variables, sums, products, infinity, Euler's number, exponentials and logarithms, with lazy-initialized interactive plots and an ELI-5 rendering.
nodes.languageNotes: Ships inline JS (no separate module): loadMathIModule plus lazy plot-update functions that render the interactive plots on IntersectionObserver and re-theme via getThemeColor.

nodes.name: initPhaseSpace
nodes.summary: Runs every registered demo initializer once the blog post is fully loaded, wrapping each in try/catch so one failing demo never breaks the others.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Appends a demo initialization function to the local inits array that initPhaseSpace later executes, forming the self-contained component registry.

nodes.name: boot
nodes.summary: Entry point for the geometry-ii inline demos: wires slider inputs to their Plotly readers and lazily mounts the projection, SVD, SVD, descent, convolution, and symmetry interactives and sets up Plotly react handlers.

nodes.name: projRead
nodes.summary: Re-renders the orthogonal-projection plot: computes the shadow of a point onto a tilted line, the perpendicular residual, and the explained (R^2) fraction as sliders move.

nodes.name: svdRead
nodes.summary: Re-renders the SVD plot showing the unit circle and its rotate-stretch-rotate image ellipse, with the two singular-vector axes and the resulting rank and condition number.

nodes.name: desRead
nodes.summary: Re-renders the descent plot: an anisotropic loss bowl with oval level-set contours and the -gradient arrow always perpendicular to the contour, reporting the gradient magnitude and condition number.

nodes.name: convRead
nodes.summary: Re-renders the convolution interactive: applies a draggable 3-tap kernel as a sliding dot product in the time domain and shows the pointwise frequency-domain multiplication |F(y)|=|F(c)|.|F(x)|.

nodes.name: symRead
nodes.summary: Re-renders the symmetry plot: cyclically reorders a bag of tokens to show the equivariant per-item output moving with the input while the invariant (mean) readout stays fixed.

nodes.name: renderLinearSeparability
nodes.summary: Draws the OR-gate (linearly separable) and XOR-gate (not separable) Plotly scatter plots with a shared theme-aware layout, illustrating why a single layer cannot learn XOR.

nodes.name: loadHistoryModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that updates the loading status and calls renderLinearSeparability, returning a resolved promise so it fits the lesson module queue.

nodes.name: loadIntuitionModule
nodes.summary: Main entry point that injects the token-animation CSS and registers every visualization section (autoregressive loop, tokenizer, embedding, positional encoding, attention, FFN, residual stream, prediction) into the lazy init registry, then starts the IntersectionObserver and wires dark-mode re-rendering.

nodes.name: runAttention
nodes.summary: Computes and renders the attention demonstration: a small context vocabulary (bank/river/money) where the position of 'bank' is pulled halfway toward each other context word, drawing the attention 'handshake' lines.

nodes.name: TokenizerViz
nodes.summary: Mock tokenizer with a word vocabulary and BPE-like subword split rules; tokenizes user input and renders colored token chips with IDs and subword markers.

nodes.name: EmbeddingViz
nodes.summary: Renders word embeddings as a scatter and supports vector arithmetic (e.g. king-queen+woman) to illustrate how meaning is represented as geometry.

nodes.name: PositionalEncodingViz
nodes.summary: Visualizes sinusoidal positional encodings as a plot whose number of dimensions is slider-controlled, plus a demo showing how positional vectors are added to token embeddings.

nodes.name: FFNViz
nodes.summary: Demonstrates the feed-forward network layer with selectable scenarios (e.g. apple/fruit) to show how FFNs apply a non-linear transformation of the residual stream.

nodes.name: ResidualStreamViz
nodes.summary: Visualizes the transformer residual stream across layers, letting the user scrub to a layer and see how each sublayer adds to the accumulating signal.

nodes.name: PredictionViz
nodes.summary: Renders the final prediction head as a distribution over the next word with a temperature slider controlling the sharpness of the softmax.

nodes.name: AutoregressiveViz
nodes.summary: Animates the autoregressive generation loop, appending one predicted word at a time back into the model until the endoftext token, with a play button to run the generation.

nodes.name: buildTimeline
nodes.summary: Builds the vertical timeline of language milestones inside #timeline-container (guarded against double-build), deferring the actual DOM construction through triple requestAnimationFrame to avoid reflow corruption.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Module initializer that injects the timeline CSS and then builds the timeline, running on DOMContentLoaded (or immediately if the document is already loaded).

nodes.name: loadMathIModule
nodes.summary: Entry point for the math-i inline scripts: sets up the lazy render/plot observers and renders the interactive math plots for the numerical-foundations lesson.

nodes.name: renderELI5Math
nodes.summary: Renders the plain-language (ELI-5) explanation of the current math concept, complementing the formal notation in the lesson.

nodes.name: Basic Math Concepts II — Linear Algebra for AI
nodes.summary: PHP lesson on linear algebra for AI — vector spaces, matrices/tensors, function composition, the Hadamard product, transposition, and softmax/cross-entropy — with inline Plotly.js visualizations (1D–4D vector spaces, RGB image tensor, composition, Hadamard) that lazy-render on scroll.
nodes.languageNotes: All interactivity lives in inline <script> inside the PHP file (no separate .js); heavy 3-D Plotly surfaces are lazy-rendered via an IntersectionObserver (lazyRender/observePlot).

nodes.name: loadMathIIModule
nodes.summary: Module-queue entry point for this lesson; kicks off initialization of the Math II plot suite once loaded.

nodes.name: initDataBasics
nodes.summary: Bootstrap that runs cheap global work immediately and defers each heavy section behind a lazyInit until its container scrolls near the viewport.

nodes.name: initMathIIPlots
nodes.summary: One-time initializer that renders the Math II Plotly visualizations (BW/RGB image tensors, vector plots, composition, Hadamard, interactive vector spaces) once Plotly is available.

nodes.name: lazyRender
nodes.summary: Central lazy-render primitive: stores the latest render callback for a plot and either draws it now (if visible) or queues it for the IntersectionObserver to fire on scroll-in.

nodes.name: initInteractiveVectorSpaces

nodes.name: Statistics II — Inference and Information
nodes.summary: PHP lesson on statistical inference and information — Bayesian updating, Shannon entropy, the Dirichlet distribution, Gaussian mixtures / EM, the law of large numbers, Markov chains, Boltzmann/temperature, MLE, the chain rule, KL divergence, and bag-of-words — with interactive labs in statistics.js.

nodes.name: activationlab.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Activation Functions lesson: an explorer that plots and explains ReLU/GELU/SiLU/Sigmoid/Tanh/Leaky-ReLU/Identity, plus a Softmax lab that turns raw logits into a probability pie and bar chart.

nodes.summary: Module entry point that lazily registers the activation explorer and the Softmax lab to initialize when scrolled into view, and re-runs them on theme toggle.

nodes.name: initPureActivationLab
nodes.summary: Wires the activation-type <select> to plot the chosen function in Plotly and inject its formula and pro/con description via render_temml/renderMarkdown.

nodes.name: initSoftmaxLab
nodes.summary: Builds the Softmax widget: editable logit inputs, a donut pie and horizontal bar plot of normalized probabilities, and a step-by-step exponential calculation readout.

nodes.name: erfApprox
nodes.summary: Approximates the error function (Abramowitz & Stegun 7.1.26) so GELU can be plotted without a special-math library.

nodes.name: Activation Functions: The Neural Decision Makers
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson on why non-linearity is required (linear layers collapse), introducing the activation lab, the Softmax 'multi-class gate', the historical move from Heaviside to ReLU, and GELU/SiLU as the Transformer and diffusion standards.

nodes.name: autodiff.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Automatic Differentiation lesson: a tape-based reverse-mode AD stepper, an SVG computational-graph visualizer, a gradient-descent-on-a-loss-landscape animator, and a vanishing/exploding-gradient explorer.
nodes.languageNotes: Four demo state objects (ADTape, ADGraph, GDDemo, VGDemo) are driven through a shared lazy-load registry; each renders into Plotly or inline SVG.

nodes.name: loadAutodiffModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that lazily registers the tape demo, computational graph, gradient-descent plot, and vanishing-gradient plot to initialize in-view and re-render on theme change.

nodes.name: Automatic Differentiation: How Machines Learn
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson covering why symbolic/numerical differentiation fail at scale, the chain rule, forward vs. reverse mode, the tape with a concrete worked example, PyTorch/TensorFlow tape APIs, a from-scratch autograd engine, and the vanishing/exploding-gradient problem.

nodes.name: backproplab.js
nodes.summary: The backpropagation visualizer: a 3-4-4-2 network rendered as SVG with animated forward/backward pulses, hoverable cones of influence, click-to-expand per-neuron/weight equations with underbraces, and a full-SGD step with live weight update.
nodes.languageNotes: Single self-contained widget (renderBackpropVisual) using a unique id prefix, a seeded PRNG for deterministic reset, requestAnimationFrame pulse animation, and a symbol/underbrace LaTeX statement builder.

nodes.name: loadBackproplabModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that mounts the sigmoid derivative plot and the main backprop visualizer into the lesson.

nodes.name: renderBackpropVisual
nodes.summary: Builds the full interactive network: forward/backward math, SVG geometry, editable input/target/learning-rate fields, cone-of-influence highlighting, pulse animation, and the expandable equation panel.

nodes.name: sigmoidPlot
nodes.summary: Plots the sigmoid and its derivative in Plotly and attaches a mouse-following tangent-line overlay showing z, sigma, and sigma-prime at the hovered point.

nodes.name: Backpropagation: How a Neural Network Learns From Its Mistakes
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson introducing the 1986 backprop algorithm, walking through one neuron's forward pass, the half-SSE loss, and the chain-rule error signal, then embedding the live network visualizer.

nodes.name: derivativelab.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Derivatives lesson: plots a chosen loss landscape, shows the look-ahead secant slope, and performs a single gradient-descent step, with a plain-language 'AI decision' readout.

nodes.name: loadDerivativeModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that initializes the derivative lab and re-renders it on dark/light theme toggle.

nodes.name: initDerivativeLab
nodes.summary: Wires the function/x/h sliders to recompute the secant slope, draw the curve with secant and tangent lines, update the math breakdown, and handle the 'Take 1 Step Down' gradient-descent button.

nodes.name: Derivatives: How AI "Learns" to get better
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson framing the derivative as a 'steepness check' for finding the way downhill, introducing gradient descent, partial derivatives and the gradient vector, and the chain rule as the bridge to backpropagation.

nodes.name: differentiation.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Differentiation lesson with four demos: secant-to-tangent limit, a tangent-line explorer on x^3-3x, a chain-rule (sin(ax)) plot, and a 2D gradient-descent-on-a-surface visualizer.
nodes.languageNotes: Each demo is a standalone init function registered to its own Plotly container via a shared lazy-load registry, so they initialize independently on scroll.

nodes.name: loadDerivativesModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that lazily registers the four differentiation demos to initialize in-view and re-render on theme change.

nodes.name: initSecantTangent
nodes.summary: Demos the limit definition by dragging h toward zero, plotting f(x)=x^2 with the converging secant line and the true tangent, and showing the computed slopes in TeX.

nodes.name: initTangentLineExplorer
nodes.summary: Moves a point along f(x)=x^3-3x, drawing the tangent line and marking the critical points where f'(x)=0 (the local extrema).

nodes.name: initChainRuleDemo
nodes.summary: Visualizes the chain rule on f(x)=sin(ax), plotting the function and its derivative a*cos(ax) while labeling the outer and inner derivatives.

nodes.name: initGradientSurface
nodes.summary: Shows the 2D gradient of f(x,y)=x^2+y^2 as a contour plot with a red arrow pointing in the negative-gradient (descent) direction, updated by two sliders.

nodes.name: Differentiation: The Mathematics of Change
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson on the derivative from the Newton/Leibniz history through the limit definition, the differentiation rules (with the chain rule flagged as the foundation of backprop), partial derivatives, and the gradient vector, with four interactive demos.

nodes.name: Hyperparameters: The Numbers You Choose
nodes.summary: Part 2 prose lesson distinguishing learned parameters from chosen hyperparameters, explaining why they cannot be solved for, and surveying how they are actually found: expert transfer, scaling laws, grid/random search, Bayesian optimization, and multi-fidelity search (with a note on the OmniOpt tool).

nodes.name: losslab.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Loss lesson: a Mean-Squared-Error 'loss bowl' with live slope, and a cross-entropy explorer that splits a softmax-style output vector across Cat/Dog/Bird and shows the log-loss and confidence verdict.

nodes.name: loadLossModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that initializes the loss lab and re-renders it on theme toggle.

nodes.name: initLossLab
nodes.summary: Wires the MSE and cross-entropy sliders to recompute the loss and derivative, render the loss-bowl and log-loss plots, and update the classification-confidence status.

nodes.name: Loss: Teaching through Failure
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson on loss functions: Mean Squared Error for regression, cross-entropy for classification, Goodhart's Law, and the deep insight that cross-entropy is Shannon entropy and pairs with softmax to give a clean (y_hat - y) gradient.

nodes.name: minimalneuron.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Smallest-Network lesson: builds a single-neuron tf.sequential linear model (y=ax+b) with TF.js, trains it with SGD in a live loop, and plots the fitted line, loss history, and current weights.
nodes.languageNotes: Self-contained MinimalLab namespace plus global toggleTraining/initBlock dispatchers; uses lazy IntersectionObserver init and an async epoch loop with tf.nextFrame for smooth updates.

nodes.name: loadMinimalNeuronModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that lazily registers MinimalLab.init to run when the data chart scrolls into view, and re-runs it on theme change.

nodes.name: MinimalLab
nodes.summary: Namespace holding the single-neuron config and the init / toggleTraining / updateVisuals logic that builds, trains, and plots the y=ax+b model.

nodes.name: Smallest possible neural network
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson introducing the neuron as y=ax+b (weight and bias), the training loop (predict, loss, gradient descent), random initialization to break symmetry, the mirror-rule for output layers, and the statistical/linear-algebra nature of learning, with a TF.js/PyTorch code tab.

nodes.name: optimizerlab.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Optimizer lesson: a 1D loss-landscape simulator that steps through SGD, SGD+Momentum, and Adam, logging each step, detecting convergence/divergence, and plotting the optimization path.
nodes.languageNotes: Optimizer memory (velocity, Adam m/v/t) lives in module-level let state shared across run/pause/reset; the update loop runs on setInterval and color-codes the gradient magnitude.

nodes.name: loadOptimizerModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that initializes the optimizer lab controls and plot.

nodes.name: initOptimizerLab
nodes.summary: Sets up the optimizer-type selector, learning-rate (with a high-LR warning), start-position, and epochs controls, redrawing the landscape plot as the user adjusts them.

nodes.name: startOptimizer
nodes.summary: Runs the selected optimizer (SGD/Momentum/Adam) in a setInterval loop, applying each update rule, logging steps, and stopping on convergence, divergence, or the epoch limit.

nodes.name: The Optimizer: Navigating the Loss Landscape
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson comparing SGD, Momentum, and Adam on a 1D loss landscape: the update-rule math for each, the Robbins-Monro/Cauchy history, why Adam's per-parameter adaptivity dominates (Zipf), and a table of common pitfalls.

nodes.name: Reinforcement Learning
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson on the math of RL: MDPs, value/Q functions and the Bellman equation, Q-learning, policy gradients and REINFORCE, actor-critic/PPO, and the LLM-alignment methods RLHF, DPO, and GRPO, plus reward hacking and open problems.
nodes.languageNotes: Static prose lesson; defines an inline loadReinforcementLearningModule() in a <script> block (no external JS module).

nodes.name: traininglab.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Live-Training lesson: a TrainLab namespace that builds a small TF.js ReLU network on an XOR-like dataset, trains it live, and renders the decision-boundary contour, loss history, per-row predictions, weight heatmaps, and a LaTeX forward-pass equation monitor.
nodes.languageNotes: TrainLab is layered into public API / orchestrators / concrete tasks / atomic helpers; uses tf.browser.toPixels for weight heatmaps and render_temml for the live equations.

nodes.name: loadTrainingModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that initializes the training module (setting up the IntersectionObserver that starts TrainLab when the dashboard is visible).

nodes.name: initTrainingModule
nodes.summary: Creates an IntersectionObserver that calls TrainLab.init('traininglab') the first time the lab dashboard scrolls into view, falling back to immediate init if no target exists.

nodes.name: TrainLab
nodes.summary: Namespace encapsulating the live-training lab: model build/compile, the async training loop, and all visualization (decision boundary, loss chart, prediction table, weight heatmaps, and the LaTeX math monitor).

nodes.name: Live Training of a Neural Network
nodes.summary: Part 2 lesson combining tensors, activations, and a model into a live training dashboard: a 2-input ReLU network trained on a small XOR-like dataset, with a decision-boundary map, live weights/heatmaps, and a full forward-pass equation monitor.

nodes.name: computer_vision.js
nodes.summary: Interactive convolution and feature-map explorer for the 'What Machines See' lesson. Runs TF.js convolutions over a stop-sign image, renders a multi-filter edge-detection grid plus a combined heatmap, and computes per-pixel convolution math on hover.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy TF.js tensor usage guarded by manual rank/shape console.assert helpers; IntersectionObserver lazy init; theme-aware redraw via __MN_DARK.onChange.

nodes.name: applyConv2D
nodes.summary: Low-level TF.js 2D convolution over a rank-4 input with an optional 180-degree kernel flip; the shared building block for single- and multi-channel convolutions.

nodes.name: applyMultiChannelConv
nodes.summary: Splits a source canvas into RGB channels, convolves each independently with the user kernel, and re-stacks the clipped result into an image tensor.

nodes.name: setKernel
nodes.summary: Public API called from the lesson's preset buttons; loads a kernel matrix into the input grid, resizes it, and re-runs the convolution.

nodes.name: initVisionLab
nodes.summary: Sets up the source-image canvas, the editable kernel table, and the mouse handlers that drive the focus overlay, crosshair, pixel tooltip, and live convolution math.

nodes.name: buildConvLatex
nodes.summary: Builds the per-pixel weighted-sum LaTeX (RGB column vectors times kernel weights) rendered in the live math box.

nodes.name: loadComputerVisionModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point; lazy-registers the convolution explorer and the FeatureLab behind an IntersectionObserver and wires dark/light redraws.

nodes.name: FeatureLab
nodes.summary: Global feature-map lab: applies four orientation-tuned edge filters to the grayscale image and combines their squared activations into a multi-edge corner/shape heatmap.

nodes.name: What Machines See
nodes.summary: Lesson covering the whole vision stack: the convolution mechanism, the feature hierarchy, the full CNN pipeline (with PyTorch and TensorFlow reference code), and the task ladder from classification to detection, segmentation (U-Net, Mask R-CNN, SAM), Vision Transformers (ViT/MAE/CLIP), and 3D.

nodes.name: Pixels and Checkerboards
nodes.summary: Lesson on transposed convolutions (deconvolution) and the checkerboard upsampling artifact, grounded in Odena et al. 2016, with the two standard fixes: resize-conv and jitter.

nodes.name: deeplearninglab.js
nodes.summary: Deep-learning playground exposing a global DeepLab object: trains TF.js models live for linear regression, AND, and XOR, and renders loss curves, decision-boundary contours, and per-layer weight heatmaps.
nodes.languageNotes: Object-literal module (DeepLab) with method-style API; tf.sequential models, per-epoch fit loop, and Plotly charts; lazy IntersectionObserver init.

nodes.name: DeepLab
nodes.summary: Global deep-learning lab: builds sequential TF.js models, trains them one epoch at a time, and renders loss plots, decision-boundary contour maps, live predictions, and weight heatmaps.

nodes.name: loadDeepLearningModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point; lazy-inits the linear-regression and deep-network blocks via IntersectionObserver and wires theme-change re-renders.

nodes.name: Deep Learning
nodes.summary: Lesson from a single neuron to deep networks: layer composition, the Universal Approximation Theorem, why depth beats width (reuse), backpropagation, residual connections, and the optimizer's implicit bias (saddle points, grokking, double descent).

nodes.name: Inceptionism: What the Network Sees
nodes.summary: Lesson on Inceptionism/DeepDream: freezing the weights and running gradient ascent on an image to reveal the shapes and objects a network stores (bananas, the weightlifter's dumbbells, dream maps, fractal dreams) as engineered pareidolia.

nodes.name: normalizationlab.js
nodes.summary: Layer-Normalization and Group-Normalization labs: a global NormLab object that renders the step-by-step mean/variance/standardize/scale-shift math with live gamma/beta controls and bar plots, plus an interactive group-regrouping heatmap.
nodes.languageNotes: Object-literal NormLab plus a separate initGroupNormLab closure that manages its own local helper functions and DOM tables.

nodes.name: NormLab
nodes.summary: Global LayerNorm lab: computes per-row mean and variance, renders the three-step normalization arithmetic per feature, and plots raw versus normalized feature bars.

nodes.name: initGroupNormLab
nodes.summary: Builds the GroupNorm demo: 8 channels x 16 spatial positions, a G slider that regroups channels, input/output heatmaps, and per-group mean/std stat cards.

nodes.name: loadNormalizationModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point; lazy-inits NormLab and the GroupNorm lab via IntersectionObserver and wires theme-change re-renders.

nodes.name: Understanding Layer Normalization
nodes.summary: Lesson on Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016): the mean/variance/standardize/scale-shift math, its role in GPT pre-norm, RNNs, and ViTs, the geometric 'projection onto a sphere' view, and Group Normalization as the diffusion-model default.

nodes.name: origami.js
nodes.summary: Interactive demos for 'Origami in N Dimensions': ReLU networks as paper-folds, including the non-separable egg, the ReLU hyperplane hammer, 1-D/3-D folding, the exponential region cascade, shear/peeling, bimodal tuning, and the poker-hand causal validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Global OG registry/observer plus a family of ogInit* demo functions; canvas 2D drawing with a small hand-rolled 2x2 linear-algebra helper set; Plotly for the poker/tuning/egg3 plots.

nodes.name: OG
nodes.summary: Global demo registry and palette manager: theme-aware color palettes, IntersectionObserver-based lazy init, and dark/light redraw and data-regen hooks.

nodes.name: ogInitNonsep
nodes.summary: Non-separability demo: generate egg/XOR/spiral/blob data and let the reader drag a straight line to see why no single flat boundary can separate a surrounded class.

nodes.name: ogInitFold3d
nodes.summary: 3-D fold demo: three ReLU hyperplanes fold the 2-D egg into a lifted tent so a single flat plane separates the classes, with drag-to-rotate and an animate-the-fold control.

nodes.name: ogInitCascade
nodes.summary: Renders the piecewise-linear region mosaic of a small deep ReLU net, showing how the number of linear regions grows as N^L with depth.

nodes.name: ogInitShear
nodes.summary: 'Peeling the orange' demo: shears off one slice of the outer class per layer with tilted hyperplanes, the inefficient no-spare-dimension alternative to folding.

nodes.name: ogInitPoker
nodes.summary: Poker-hand validation plots: representation dimensionality rising through layers, the Hartigan dip (bimodality) distribution growing during training, and the silencing causality test.

nodes.name: loadOrigamiModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point; registers all origami demos with the lazy observer and wires dark/light redraws of the registered draw functions.

nodes.name: Origami in N Dimensions
nodes.summary: Lesson (Keup & Helias 2022) that a stack of dense ReLU layers manufactures linear separability by progressively folding the data manifold into unoccupied higher dimensions, tying the picture to the fold-and-cut theorem, the inefficient shear alternative, and a poker-hand causal validation.

nodes.name: overandunderfittinglab.js
nodes.summary: Over/under-fitting lab exposing a global FittingLab object: fits a polynomial-regression model on noisy sin(x) with adjustable degree, noise, and L2, and plots the model against ground truth to expose the bias-variance tradeoff and the extrapolation trap.
nodes.languageNotes: Object-literal FittingLab with a TF.js single-dense model over an explicit polynomial feature expansion and a custom MSE+L2 loss.

nodes.name: FittingLab
nodes.summary: Global fitting lab: generates noisy sine data, fits a polynomial via TF.js with an optional L2 penalty, and plots training/test fit, ground truth, and the model curve with the training window shaded.

nodes.name: loadOverAndUnderFittingModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point; lazy-inits the fitting lab via IntersectionObserver.

nodes.name: Over- and underfitting
nodes.summary: Lesson on the bias-variance tradeoff using polynomial regression on a sine wave: the MSE loss, gradient descent with Adam, the extrapolation failure (a metaphor for LLM hallucination), L1/L2 regularization, dropout, Runge's phenomenon, and double descent.

nodes.name: resnetlab.js
nodes.summary: ResNet lab exposing a global ResNetLab object: plots gradient strength versus depth for a plain (multiplicative, vanishing) network against a residual (additive, preserved) network, and draws an SVG residual-block architecture diagram.
nodes.languageNotes: Object-literal ResNetLab; Plotly gradient plot plus a hand-built inline SVG architecture diagram with identity/projection arcs.

nodes.name: ResNetLab
nodes.summary: Global ResNet lab: computes and plots the multiplicative-vs-additive gradient decay and renders the residual-block architecture diagram with skip-connection arcs and tensor-shape labels.

nodes.name: loadResnetModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point; lazy-inits the gradient-comparison plot via IntersectionObserver.

nodes.name: Deep Learning Mechanics: ResNets & Vanishing Gradients
nodes.summary: Lesson on the vanishing-gradient problem and the ResNet residual shortcut: the multiplicative chain rule, the identity 'gradient superhighway' (d(F+x)/dx = dF/dx + 1), and 1x1 convolutions for projection shortcuts.

nodes.name: topology.js
nodes.summary: Interactive demos for 'Topology and the Geometry of Thought': live TF.js tanh/ReLU networks untangling the 2-D egg, the 1-D egg, and a click-to-build spiral, painting decision grids and live hidden-layer representations.
nodes.languageNotes: Global TOP registry/observer plus tpInit* demo functions; live tf.sequential nets trained in a loop with tf.nextFrame yielding; canvas 2D decision-grid painting.

nodes.name: TOP
nodes.summary: Global demo registry and palette manager: theme-aware colors, IntersectionObserver-based lazy init, and dark/light redraw hooks shared by all topology demos.

nodes.name: buildNet
nodes.summary: Builds a 2-layer TF.js classification net (dense hidden layer with the chosen activation plus a sigmoid output) compiled with Adam and binary cross-entropy.

nodes.name: paintDecisionGrid
nodes.summary: Paints the model's decision boundary as a fine colored grid across the canvas and overlays the data points, used by all three demos to show separation live.

nodes.name: tpInitEgg
nodes.summary: Topological lower-bound demo: trains a width-2 (doomed) versus width-3 (escapes) tanh net on the 2-D egg to show that a third hidden unit breaks the enclosure.

nodes.name: tpInitPlay
nodes.summary: 'Build your own data' demo: click to add points, a continuously-training net, and a live hidden-layer representation panel cycling through neuron pairs.

nodes.name: loadTopologyModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point; registers all topology demos with the lazy observer and wires dark/light redraws of the registered draw functions.

nodes.name: Topology and the Geometry of Thought
nodes.summary: Lesson (Olah 2014) that a smooth (tanh/sigmoid) layer is a homeomorphism - it can stretch and squish but never cut, tear, or fold - and therefore a network's power is bounded by its width, since a surrounded class needs an extra dimension to escape.

nodes.name: algorithms.js
nodes.summary: Interactive visualization module for the 'How Transformers Execute Algorithms' lesson. Renders step-by-step Fourier-based modular addition, in-context algorithm execution (LLM tracing addition/multiplication/GCD), algorithmic prompting (Zhou et al. 2022), and wave interference demos using Plotly and Canvas 2D.
nodes.languageNotes: Four top-level render* functions; each builds a self-contained interactive widget into a container div. Uses global `themeColor()` and `temml` (TeX renderer) from the blog base. DOMContentLoaded bootstrap auto-invokes all four widgets if their container divs exist.

nodes.name: renderFourierAlgorithm
nodes.summary: Renders the 12-step interactive walkthrough of the Nanda et al. (2023) Fourier algorithm for modular addition: embedding on circles, addition theorems via attention, unembedding, multi-frequency constructive interference, softmax, and an interactive playground with frequency toggles.

nodes.name: renderICLExecution
nodes.summary: Simulates in-context algorithm execution: shows how an LLM traces columnar addition, repeated-addition multiplication, or Euclidean GCD token-by-token, with residual-stream state panel, layer-activity bars (parsing/binding/execution), and step/execute/Animate controls.

nodes.name: renderAlgorithmicPrompting
nodes.summary: Tabbed visualization of the Zhou et al. (2022) algorithmic-prompting findings: the ambiguity problem (few-shot vs. algorithmic prompt), the specificity spectrum (0.5%→90.5% on 19-digit addition), the four teaching stages, and the proof-of-execution experiments with an error-injection canvas chart.

nodes.name: renderWaveInterference
nodes.summary: Interactive Plotly demo of two sine waves and their sum, with a phase-shift slider and constructive/destructive/quadrature presets; explains the same interference principle the trained Transformer uses across its 5 Fourier frequencies.

nodes.name: How Transformers Execute Algorithms
nodes.summary: Part 4 lesson on how a one-layer Transformer discovers the Discrete Fourier Transform for modular addition (Nanda et al. 2023 grokking), covering the 5-step algorithm, W_L neuron-logit map, Fourier sparsity of W_E, in-context algorithm execution (Garg 2022, Zhou 2022), digit-wise number representations (Levy & Geva 2024), counting limits (Fu 2024, Conde 2025), and the transformer-as-state-machine view (Hahn 2020). Embeds inline Plotly scripts plus the algorithms.js widgets.

nodes.name: Beyond Transformers (Mamba, RWKV, RetNet)
nodes.summary: Part 4 survey lesson on sub-quadratic Transformer alternatives: state-space models (S4, Mamba, Mamba-2/SSD, Jamba), linear attention (Performer, RetNet), RWKV, Hyena, Mega, Mixture-of-Depths, with compute/memory comparison tables and where Transformers still win. nodes.name: The Semantic Tug-of-War: How Transformers 'Think'

nodes.name: loadDiffusionModule

nodes.name: buildColorFrames

nodes.name: mountNoiseSlider

nodes.name: makeTokenizerViz

nodes.name: makeCrossAttentionViz
nodes.summary: Builds an interactive cross-attention widget where clicking a prompt word highlights the region of the astronaut image that word would attend to during denoising, illustrating how text tokens condition the U-Net.

nodes.name: embeddinglab.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the 'Embeddings: The Geometry of Meaning' lesson (Part 4, order 4). ~8650 lines of vanilla JS that renders ~25 distinct visualizations of embedding-space geometry: 1D/2D/3D word spaces, vector arithmetic, dot-product/cosine similarity, rotational and scale invariance, parallelogram law, Riemannian manifolds, cross-lingual alignment, metric tensors, anisotropy, superposition, negation, in-context learning, hyperbolic (Poincare) embeddings, and canvas-based topology (Voronoi, persistent homology, polytopes, grammar-as-rotation).
nodes.languageNotes: No in-project imports; pairs with embeddinglab.php lesson. Uses dual rendering backends (ECharts GL + Plotly for 3D scatter/surface, raw Canvas 2D for topology/homology/polytope/grammar). Lazy-loads every widget through an IntersectionObserver registry (_embLazyRegister) so heavy plots only render when scrolled into view, and re-renders all on dark/light theme change via window.__MN_DARK.

nodes.name: loadEmbeddingModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point satisfying the blog's load*Module() queue contract. Sets up the embedding-space IntersectionObserver, calls initEmbeddingEditor() eagerly, registers all ~20 other visualizations via _embLazyRegister, starts the lazy observer, and hooks window.__MN_DARK to re-render everything on theme toggle.

nodes.name: _getEC3D
nodes.summary: Caches and initializes one ECharts GL instance per plot div (purging any prior Plotly chart and its loading spinner first), attaching a ResizeObserver so each 3D embedding plot resizes with its container.

nodes.name: _embLazyRegister
nodes.summary: Registers a (elementId, initFn) pair into the lazy-render registry; _embLazyCreateObserver then attaches a single IntersectionObserver that runs each initFn once when its plot scrolls into view, deferring heavy 3D/canvas work until needed.

nodes.name: renderSpace
nodes.summary: Renders one of the 1D/2D/3D 'evolution' embedding spaces from the evoSpaces data (temperature scale, gender/power plane, human/animal/divine 3D space) as a labeled scatter, with optional highlighted token and animated vector-step traces.

nodes.name: renderComparison3D
nodes.summary: Renders a side-by-side 3D comparison of selected tokens (e.g. Man/King/Lion) and computes pairwise metrics (Euclidean distance, cosine similarity, angle) shown in a stats panel to compare how geometry encodes relations.

nodes.name: calcEvo
nodes.summary: Drives the vector-arithmetic calculator (e.g. King - Man + Woman = Queen): parses a small expression grammar over named tokens, applies the vector ops, and renders the resulting displacement in the space with a live result readout.

nodes.name: initEmbeddingEditor
nodes.summary: Builds the editable embedding tables (one row per word with per-dimension inputs) and wires add/remove/update handlers so a reader can mutate word vectors and watch dependent plots respond.

nodes.name: renderDotProductLab
nodes.summary: Interactive two-vector lab where sliders set each vector's angle/magnitude and the plot updates live to show the dot product, cosine similarity, and the angle between vectors, tying the inner product to semantic alignment.

nodes.name: renderRotationalInvariance
nodes.summary: Visualizes that cosine similarity / relative geometry is invariant to a global rotation of the embedding space, rotating the whole word cloud and showing similarity values are preserved.

nodes.name: renderParallelogram
nodes.summary: Demonstrates the parallelogram law of vector addition for word-analogy concepts (royalty, gender, etc.), drawing the completed parallelogram and the landing vertex for A - B + C style relations.

nodes.name: renderManifoldVisualization
nodes.summary: Illustrates the manifold hypothesis by projecting word embeddings onto a curved low-dimensional surface embedded in a higher-dimensional ambient space, with intrinsic coordinates (u,v) and a z-surface.

nodes.name: renderCrossLingualFrame
nodes.summary: 2D cross-lingual alignment visual (English/Japanese) showing two language frames that can be rotated into alignment, with an animate/reset control to demonstrate how the two spaces share structure.

nodes.name: renderDualManifolds
nodes.summary: Renders two 3D parametric surfaces (English and Japanese manifolds) and frames translation as path-finding between corresponding points on the dual surfaces, with rotation/separation controls and an alignment animation.

nodes.name: renderMetricTensor
nodes.summary: Visualizes a local metric tensor that warps the embedding space (an 'attention warping' picture), showing how distances/similarities are rescaled anisotropically across the space.

nodes.name: renderScaleInvariance
nodes.summary: Shows that normalizing vectors to the unit sphere makes cosine similarity invariant to magnitude, with a magnitude slider demonstrating that scaling a vector does not change its directional similarity.

nodes.name: renderPlatonicHypothesis
nodes.summary: Illustrates the Platonic representation hypothesis: different models/tasks converge on shared 'Platonic' directions in embedding space, with a control to select a module position and show alignment of directions.

nodes.name: initAnisotropy
nodes.summary: Sets up the anisotropy visualization, generating an anisotropic (coned) set of word vectors and a control to compare the narrow cosine distribution of real embeddings against an isotropic baseline.

nodes.name: renderSuperposition
nodes.summary: Demonstrates superposition / polysemanticity by showing a single direction encoding several simultaneously-active features (a 'polyseme' vector), with a slider controlling how many features share one dimension.

nodes.name: renderNegation
nodes.summary: Visualizes negation as a direction in embedding space, letting the reader pick a negation word and see the negated position of a concept (e.g. 'not hot') plotted against the original.

nodes.name: initICL
nodes.summary: Initializes the in-context-learning visualization, building a task-vector picture where a prompt's examples steer the embedding toward an answer, with a prompt panel and controls to inspect the steering vector.

nodes.name: renderHyperbolicEmbedding
nodes.summary: Lays out a hierarchical tree inside the Poincare disk and renders geodesics/distances in hyperbolic geometry, with a curvature slider to show how hierarchy packs into a bounded disk.

nodes.name: initTopologyCones
nodes.summary: Sets up the 'narrow cones' topology visualization, sampling token-vector points and their local cone angles across a dimension slider to show how high-dimensional clusters look like thin cones.

nodes.name: renderFractalFolding
nodes.summary: Shows semantic folding / fractal self-similarity: zooming into a cluster reveals the same structure at smaller scale, with a zoom slider illustrating self-similar organization of the embedding space.

nodes.name: initHolographic
nodes.summary: Sets up the holographic-information-storage demo, where damaging a fraction of a token's dimensions still leaves meaning recoverable from the surviving ones, with a damage slider and before/after similarity stats.

nodes.name: initVoronoi
nodes.summary: Builds an interactive Voronoi-cell partition of the 2D embedding plane on a canvas: clicking a point shows its owning seed/word and cell, with a legend and stats on cell areas as a picture of decision regions in meaning-space.

nodes.name: initHomology
nodes.summary: Computes and renders persistent homology of token-vector clouds on a canvas: a 3D point cloud, a scale (filtration) slider, and a persistence barcode tracking which loops/cavities (holes) in meaning-space survive across scale.

nodes.name: initPolytope
nodes.summary: Computes convex hulls of token groups and renders the resulting polytopes with click-to-inspect, a legend, and a 'dilemma' list of words falling in overlapping hulls, framing the hulls as boundaries of the conceivable.

nodes.name: initGrammarRotation
nodes.summary: Demonstrates grammar as rotation operators in embedding space: conjugation/tense/pair relations act as consistent rotations, with pair highlighting and stats showing that the same rotation maps many word pairs.

nodes.name: Embeddings: The Geometry of Meaning
nodes.summary: Lesson on word embeddings as geometry: embedding-space lookup from token IDs, vector arithmetic, Euclidean vs cosine similarity, cross-lingual and platonic alignment, anisotropy, superposition, hyperbolic/Poincare embeddings, topology, Voronoi cells, persistent homology, and grammar-as-rotation, each with an interactive canvas/plotly visualization.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure PHP/HTML+Markdown lesson; ships no companion JS module in this batch (its interactive handlers reference functions defined elsewhere).

nodes.name: Where 'Paris' Lives — How an LLM Retrieves a Fact

nodes.name: initInductionHead
nodes.summary: Builds the canvas demo of the induction-head circuit: a previous-token head (layer 0) writes predecessor info into the residual stream and an induction head (layer 1) completes the [A]B...A → B pattern, illustrating K-composition.

nodes.name: initGrokking
nodes.summary: Simulates grokking of modular addition: a training-progress slider drives simulated train/test accuracy and Fourier-coherence curves through memorization, circuit-formation, and cleanup phases, with a clock-style Fourier representation.

nodes.name: initOthelloDemo
nodes.summary: Interactive Othello-GPT world-model demo: a playable board plus linear vs nonlinear probes of the internal board state and a causal intervention that flips a tile to show the next-move prediction depends on the hidden state.

nodes.name: initLinearRepDemo
nodes.summary: Draws concept directions in unembedding space and interpolates between Euclidean and causal geometry, showing that under the causal inner product causally separable concepts become orthogonal.

nodes.name: initLoopedTFDemo
nodes.summary: Steps through FLEQ-style programs (addition, countdown) as a looped transformer 'computer', animating program counter, scratchpad, and memory each clock tick to show a constant-depth transformer can emulate a general-purpose computer.

nodes.name: mechanistic_interpretability.js
nodes.summary: Canvas-based interactive module for the Mechanistic Interpretability lesson, bundling five demos: induction heads, grokking, the Othello-GPT world model, linear representations/ causal inner product, and a looped-transformer computer, plus low-level drawing and linear-algebra utilities.
nodes.languageNotes: Wrapped in an IIFE with 'use strict'; exposes only via self-invoked init/initAll rather than a loadXModule entry point.

nodes.name: Mechanistic Interpretability
nodes.summary: Lesson on reverse-engineering transformers: circuits, the residual-stream communication bus, QK/OV and Q/K/V composition, communication channels, superposition, sparse autoencoders, activation patching, the logit lens, grokking, Othello-GPT, the linear representation hypothesis, looped transformers, circuit tracing, and interpretability-driven safety.

nodes.name: Multimodal & Vision-Language Models

nodes.name: positionalembeddingslab.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for positional embeddings: unit-circle and sine/cosine wave explorers, the sinusoidal positional-encoding lab (adding a PE vector to 'king'), a repetition starburst, and a 3D PE helix manifold, all lazy-initialized via IntersectionObserver.

nodes.name: Positional Embeddings

nodes.name: Networks with Memory

nodes.name: loadSamplingLabModule

nodes.name: Temperature & Sampling

nodes.name: loadTokenizerModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that sets up a sticky-input IntersectionObserver, reveal-on-scroll observers for the method cards, and initial rendering of the tokenization failure demo.

nodes.name: tokenizerlab.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Tokenization lesson: a live master input feeds side-by-side visualizations of word-level, n-gram, character, WordPiece, and BPE tokenization, plus a 'why LLMs can't count letters' BPE demo.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a BPETokenizer class and tokenColor/escapeHtml helpers defined in shared base JS; reveal logic via IntersectionObserver.

nodes.name: Tokenization: How Words become Numbers
nodes.summary: Lesson on tokenization: a sticky input drives five methods (word-level, n-gram, character, WordPiece, BPE) with history of each, the BPE-as-compression/Zipf's-law rationale, and a demo of why models can't count letters.

nodes.name: transformer.js
nodes.summary: Core interactive module for the 'Architecture of Meaning' lesson: implements a decoder-only transformer from scratch in the browser (causal multi-head attention, pre-LN, FFN/GELU, sinusoidal positional encoding, unembedding/softmax), trains it on a user-typed corpus via TensorFlow.js, and renders a large suite of visualizations (embedding space, migration/trajectory plots, attention web, parameter sunburst, vector math).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses global state on `window` (currentWeights, persistentEmbeddingSpace, isTraining) plus module-local registries (Maps) for lazy viewport-gated rendering. Hand-rolled 2D-array linear algebra (matMul/softmax/matAdd) for the visual path, and a parallel TensorFlow.js tensor path (convert_weights_to_tensors / convert_tensors_to_weights) for actual gradient training. Entry point is async loadTransformerModule(). Integrates with optional globals AttentionEngine, Prov (provenance), TDALive (topology), Plotly, and ECharts.

nodes.name: The Architecture of Meaning: A Deep Dive into Transformers
nodes.summary: Part 4 flagship lesson that assembles tokenization, embedding, positional encoding, attention, FFN, unembedding, loss and optimizer into one trainable machine. Prose derives each equation (causal mask, multi-head attention, residual recurrence, temperature/softmax, KV-cache, MoE, induction/syntax heads) and interleaves the live transformers demo, a topological-data-analysis (TDA) attractor/repeller panel, and hyperparameter sliders.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard lesson contract (line-1 include functions.php + COURSE_METADATA block). Loads many auxiliary scripts (llm_river.js, stickybar_transformer.js, attention_engine.js, provenance.js, tda_live.js, transformer_layer_summary.js) and drives the JS demo via inline oninput/onclick handlers. Heavy use of topic-block/optional-md progressive disclosure and LaTeX in .md blocks.

nodes.name: loadTransformerModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point invoked by the blog loader: initializes the vector-math observer, updates the train-button/architecture-validity UI, runs the initial demo, and wires the master-token input to a debounced re-run.

nodes.name: run_transformer_demo
nodes.summary: Top-level orchestration of the live demo: tokenizes the training and master inputs, renders the BPE/token visualization, runs the full network forward pass with visualization, refreshes the parameter count, and snapshots state for the TDA live panel.

nodes.name: run_and_visualize_network
nodes.summary: Core inference/visualization driver: reads the architecture config, validates dimensions, reinitializes weights if the config changed, runs pre-attention visualizations, executes the forward pass with per-layer migration/trajectory plots, and renders the final probability distribution over the master tokens.

nodes.name: causalMultiHeadAttention
nodes.summary: Computes masked multi-head attention on plain 2D arrays: projects to Q/K/V, slices per head, builds the scaled dot-product score matrix, applies the causal (-1e9) mask, softmax-normalizes each row, and returns per-head Q/K/V/scores/weights/context (the weighted value sums).

nodes.name: forwardOneLayer
nodes.summary: Executes one decoder block: pre-LayerNorm, causal multi-head attention with residual add (h_attn), then a second pre-LN + FFN with residual add (h_out); optionally drives the AttentionEngine and FFN-equation renderers for a single layer's on-screen visualization.

nodes.name: runSimpleForwardPass
nodes.summary: Runs the full forward pass over N layers from an embedded+PE input, returning the final hidden-state matrix; when asked, records every intermediate (norms, projections, FFN internals) under a provenance namespace so h_last can be traced back to the input.

nodes.name: embedTokensWithPE
nodes.summary: Looks up each token in the persistent embedding table and adds its sinusoidal positional encoding, producing the initial hidden state h_0 (Batch x Length x d_model) used to start the forward pass.

nodes.name: computePositionalEncoding
nodes.summary: Computes the sinusoidal positional-encoding vector (sin/cos over the 10000^(2i/d) frequency bands) for a given position, scaled by posEmbedScalar, matching the Vaswani et al. formula.

nodes.name: addPositionalEncoding
nodes.summary: Adds the computed sinusoidal positional encoding to a token's embedding vector element-wise to form the position-tagged hidden state.

nodes.name: softmax
nodes.summary: Numerically stable softmax: subtracts the max logit before exponentiating to prevent overflow, then normalizes to a probability distribution.

nodes.name: matMul
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled matrix multiplication (with optional bias) over plain 2D arrays; the primitive used by projections, FFN, and unembedding in the visualization code path.

nodes.name: geluApprox
nodes.summary: Approximates the GELU activation via 0.5x(1+erf(x/sqrt(2))) using an erf approximation; the FFN nonlinearity (nanoGPT-style) in the visual forward pass.

nodes.name: calculateLayerNorm
nodes.summary: Applies layer normalization (mean/variance across the feature axis) with learnable gamma/beta to a hidden-state matrix, the Pre-LN operation preceding both the attention and FFN sublayers.

nodes.name: run_ffn_block
nodes.summary: Runs the feed-forward sublayer (W1 expand -> GELU -> W2 contract) on a hidden state and renders the step-by-step FFN equations/intermediate values for the selected layer.

nodes.name: get_init_weights
nodes.summary: Builds the full per-layer parameter structure for a decoder-only transformer (two pre-LNs, Q/K/V/output attention projections, FFN W1/W2 and biases, d_ff = 4*d_model) with randomly initialized weights.

nodes.name: get_or_init_embeddings
nodes.summary: Lazily builds (or returns) the persistent token->vector embedding space for the current vocabulary, seeding random embeddings for any tokens not yet present.

nodes.name: show_nr_of_params
nodes.summary: Counts total trainable parameters across all layers and exposes the breakdown UI (toggle + sunburst + table) so readers can see where the model's parameters live.

nodes.name: train_transformer
nodes.summary: Asynchronous training entry point: validates preconditions, sets up the session and optimizer, converts weights to TF variables, loops epochs awaiting runSingleEpoch, syncs weights back, disposes TF variables, and finalizes the session.

nodes.name: initTrainingSession
nodes.summary: Begins a training run: marks isTraining, locks the architecture/training controls so weights can't be invalidated mid-run, flips the button to 'Stop Training', and reads epochs/lr/optimizer from the UI.

nodes.name: runSingleEpoch
nodes.summary: One training epoch: builds training windows, takes a TF gradient step with gradient clipping, records the loss, renders per-window predictions, updates progress/ETA, syncs state, and captures residual/weight deltas for the TDA panel.

nodes.name: computeAndApplyGradients
nodes.summary: Runs one forward pass over the training windows through TensorFlow.js, computes cross-entropy loss against the next-token targets, backpropagates, clips gradients, and applies the optimizer update, returning the cost tensor.

nodes.name: buildCausalMask
nodes.summary: Builds the lower-triangular causal mask for a given context size, used to prevent tokens from attending to future positions during training.

nodes.name: renderLossGraph
nodes.summary: Plots the per-epoch training-loss history as a Plotly line chart in the fixed-height loss panel, updated on each synced epoch.

nodes.name: renderFinalProbabilities
nodes.summary: Computes and renders the final prediction distribution: unembeds the last hidden state into per-vocabulary logits, applies temperature, softmaxes, and builds the prediction chips and detailed logit/softmax/entropy/temperature breakdowns.

nodes.name: render_final_projection
nodes.summary: Renders the 'From Vectors to Words' section: the unembedding matrix multiplication, per-word logit dot-products, and the resulting softmax probabilities for the final hidden state.

nodes.name: tokenizeText
nodes.summary: Tokenizes raw text into token units, supporting word-wise (non-alphanumeric split) and BPE modes, the first step that turns the corpus into the integer/vector stream the model consumes.

nodes.name: transformer_tokenize_render
nodes.summary: Tokenizes the active input and renders the token chip strip (optionally into the BPE visualization container), returning the token array used by the rest of the pipeline.

nodes.name: evaluateVectorExpression
nodes.summary: Parses and evaluates a vector-math expression over word embeddings (e.g. 'king - man + woman') with a small recursive-descent parser, tracking each step and resolving the result to the nearest embedding, illustrating geometric meaning alignment.

nodes.name: renderDynamicAttentionWeb
nodes.summary: Renders the dynamic attention web: token chips with weighted arcs (drawn and hoverable) showing how strongly each token attends to each other, visualizing the attention matrix as a network.

nodes.name: render_migration_logic
nodes.summary: Renders a single layer's 'migration map' (2D/3D) showing how each token's vector moves from start to end of a layer, the central feature-space trajectory visualization, with vector-field and vector toggle support.

nodes.name: renderPositionalInjectionHtml
