nodes.summary: Renders two 3-D surfaces (English and rotated/separated Japanese) with word points (King/Queen/Man/Woman/Prince/Princess) and structural lines, visualizing translation as aligning two manifolds.

nodes.name: renderManifoldVisualization
nodes.summary: Renders the manifold hypothesis scene: a curved saddle-like 2-D sheet embedded in 3-D with word points placed on the surface to show that words live on a low-dimensional structure.

nodes.name: renderDirectionDemo
nodes.summary: Renders the semantic-direction demo for a stage ('gender' or 'power'): highlights parallel arrows (e.g. Man->Woman, King->Queen) and reports the angle/distance metrics between the direction vectors.

nodes.name: initEmbeddingEditor
nodes.summary: Builds editable token tables for each .embedding-table-container from the evoSpaces vocabulary data, enabling readers to inspect and modify word vectors.

nodes.name: restart_fcnn
nodes.summary: Debounced entry point (100 ms) that redraws the network diagram when model data or panel width changes, guarded by an md5 cache key so unchanged data is skipped.

nodes.name: draw_fcnn
nodes.summary: Main drawing routine: computes layer geometry and spacing, then draws each layer (input image, conv2d grids, dense neurons, flatten, layernorm) with weighted connections, skip connections, layer badges, and registers hover hit regions.

nodes.name: get_fcnn_data
nodes.summary: Extracts the drawable architecture from the global model: for each Dense/Flatten/LayerNorm/Conv2d layer (skipping internal skip-projection layers) returns layer names, neuron/unit counts, and meta info (input/output shapes, kernel sizes).

nodes.name: garben.html
nodes.summary: 22-slide standalone presentation on sheaves, cohomology, fiber bundles, gauge theory, Topoi and HoTT, framing a consistent worldview as a global section and LLM hallucination as a cohomological obstruction.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure markup; per-slide viz containers and Presentation.next/prev navigation are driven by external sheaves_presentation.js.

nodes.name: heads_web.js
nodes.summary: Self-contained IIFE for the 'Viele Koepfe' slide: a per-head attention table (chip rows) plus a canvas attention-web of bezier arcs over the sentence "the cat sat on the mat", with hover-to-inspect and a prev/next head stepper.
nodes.languageNotes: All logic local to one IIFE; only window.HeadsStepDemo is exposed, for presentation.js arrow-key stepping.

nodes.name: setHead
nodes.summary: Selects an attention head (with wraparound), updates the step label and caption, toggles the active table row and redraws the arc web.

nodes.name: drawArc
nodes.summary: Draws one attention arc between two word chips as a bezier curve on the canvas, with width, color and % label scaled by attention weight and hover state.

nodes.name: hott.html
nodes.summary: 12-slide standalone presentation introducing Homotopy Type Theory: types as spaces, paths as equality, type formers, univalence, HITs (the circle), equivalences, the n-type hierarchy, propositions-as-types vs truncated logic, inductive types and the real numbers.
nodes.languageNotes: Inline canvas demos (paths, univalence, HIT, equivalences, n-types) are wired in a <script> block that monkey-patches Presentation.goTo/next/prev to init/cleanup animations per slide.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Main lndw presentation deck "Wie funktionieren Large Language Modelle (LLM)?": ~45 slides from reality/patterns and classic-vs-AI coding through neurons, tokenization, embeddings, positional encoding, residual streams, attention, FFN, the probability tunnel, prediction (top-k/temperature), training, Chinese Room, hallucination and limits, with a sparkle canvas overlay.
nodes.languageNotes: Loads ~20 companion .js modules; several slides (Sonnenbahn, Klassisch vs KI, Neuron Intro, Stueckelung, Vorhersage, Iso-Tunnel) are steppable demos registered as global demo objects for presentation.js.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Largest lndw module: the intuition-step visualizations (TokenizerViz, PositionalEncodingViz, ResidualStreamViz, PredictionViz, NNApproxViz) plus steppable slide demos (NNStepDemo, TypewriterViz, NeuronIntroViz) and the loadIntuitionModule / loadIntuitionVizModule entry points and lazy IntersectionObserver registration.
nodes.languageNotes: Object-literal singletons with render/step methods; demos expose isOnSlide/canGoNext/canGoPrev/next/prev/reset so presentation.js can drive them with arrow keys.

nodes.name: TokenizerViz
nodes.summary: Subword tokenization visualizer: greedy morpheme matching against a curated German/English subword list with a BPE-style fallback for unknown spans, plus whitespace/punctuation handling and a token-chip renderer.

nodes.name: PositionalEncodingViz
nodes.summary: Sinusoidal positional-encoding explorer: plots per-dimension sin/cos curves and a position-by-dimension heatmap, plus an addition demo showing the same word gets different vectors at different positions.

nodes.name: ResidualStreamViz
nodes.summary: Canvas visualizer of the transformer residual stream across layers: per-token vector grids with per-layer Attention and FFN contribution blocks, flow/return arrows, hover/click layer selection and per-layer plain-language role descriptions.

nodes.name: PredictionViz
nodes.summary: Next-token prediction visualizer with a smooth tween engine: animates temperature and top-k steps, renders a sorted probability bar chart over a small vocabulary, and a top-k token strip.

nodes.name: NNApproxViz
nodes.summary: Function-approximation demo: fits a 1-hidden-layer ReLU net (evenly spaced hinge points) to a target function via least squares on the normal equations with Gaussian elimination, then plots target vs piecewise-linear approximation with the ReLU knees marked.

nodes.name: NNStepDemo
nodes.summary: Arrow-key stepper for the Stueckelung slide: walks the ReLU-approximation demo through 1..20 neurons on a sine and a custom waveform, with fast-mode skipping and a final image-reveal step gated on having seen the Sonnenbahn slide.

nodes.name: loadIntuitionModule
nodes.summary: Module entry point that boots the intuition-step visualizations (tokenizer, positional encoding, attention, residual stream, prediction, NN approximation) and wires their input/slider event handlers, then starts the lazy observer.

nodes.name: loadIntuitionVizModule
nodes.summary: Alternate entry point wiring the intuition-step visualizations (tokenizer, positional encoding, residual stream, prediction) and the embedding editor/space renderer to their DOM controls.

nodes.name: old/index.html
nodes.summary: Legacy standalone LLM-intuition presentation ("How LLMs Really Work - A Geometric Intuition"): a dark-themed slide deck with Three.js orbit views and inline demos, kept as an archived version of the current index.html deck.
nodes.languageNotes: Self-contained: inline CSS/JS, loads Three.js/temml/marked/highlight from CDN and defines its own Presentation-style navigation.

nodes.name: interpolation_viz.js
nodes.summary: Plotly chart distinguishing interpolation from extrapolation: known training points, a dotted true-function curve, and shaded green/red regions marking the (safer) inside range versus the (risky) outside range.
nodes.languageNotes: One IIFE that lazily renders via IntersectionObserver on first visibility.

nodes.name: renderInterpolationViz
nodes.summary: Builds and renders the interpolation-vs-extrapolation Plotly chart (traces, shaded region shapes and annotations) into the viz container.

nodes.name: intuition.js
nodes.summary: 3D Plotly visualizations for the forward pass: ForwardPassViz (tokens moving through embedding/layers/unembedding), Embedding3DViz (word clusters, semantic directions and king-man+woman arithmetic), Attention3DViz (per-layer attention lines and token displacement) and FFN3DViz (rare vs common facts as neuron activation and vector shift).
nodes.languageNotes: Object-literal singletons with render/setStep/animateAll methods; uses a seeded LCG for deterministic point clouds; initForwardPassSlides is the DOMContentLoaded entry point.

nodes.name: ForwardPassViz
nodes.summary: 3D Plotly stepper animating a sentence token-by-token through embedding, three transformer layers and unembedding, with movement trails and a target-word region, plus per-step plain-language explanations.

nodes.name: Embedding3DViz
nodes.summary: 3D word-embedding explorer: semantic cluster spheres, labeled directional axes (gender, rank, concreteness) and a step-by-step vector-arithmetic demo showing king - man + woman lands near queen.

nodes.name: Attention3DViz
nodes.summary: 3D Plotly visualizer stepping through transformer layers, showing how tokens displace and how named attention heads (syntax, subject, semantics, context, prediction) draw colored lines between tokens as context accumulates.

nodes.name: FFN3DViz
nodes.summary: 3D visualizer of the feed-forward network as a knowledge lookup: rare facts activate few neurons (short, local shift) while common patterns activate many (long, distributed shift), shown with detector neurons and an animated vector move.

nodes.name: isosurfaces.js
nodes.summary: Canvas demo of probability iso-surfaces ("Truth Tunnel"): as a story is generated token by token it draws an entropy-scaled envelope around the chosen path, small alternative branches at every token, large diverging story branches, near-impossible far words, plus a temperature/entropy HUD and step-by-step info panel.
nodes.languageNotes: Single IIFE (IsosurfaceDemo) with a tween engine (easeOutCubic) and a public stepper API (init/next/prev/reset/canGoNext/canGoPrev/isOnIsoSlide) for presentation.js.

nodes.name: IsosurfaceDemo
nodes.summary: Encapsulated demo module: owns the iso-surface scene data (prompt, generated tokens, entropy, branches, mini-splits), the tweened step state and the canvas rendering, exposing a stepper API for arrow-key navigation.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Main canvas renderer for the attention web: sizes the canvas to the container, computes chip center x-coordinates, and draws every non-diagonal attention arc for the current head, dimming arcs not touching the hovered word.

nodes.name: TypewriterViz
nodes.summary: Typewriter effect controller for the Klassisch vs. KI slide: auto-types the code panel when the slide activates and blocks navigation until typing completes.

nodes.name: NeuronIntroViz
nodes.summary: Arrow-key scene stepper for the neural-net intro slide: reveals and walks through scenes explaining dense(x)=W*x+B (weights/bias) and vectors/matrices as learnable parameters.

nodes.name: jquery.min.js
nodes.summary: Bundled/minified jQuery v3.7.1 (MIT) providing the global $ / jQuery DOM-manipulation helpers used by some lndw demos (e.g. reset_nn_num_neurons).
nodes.languageNotes: Third-party minified UMD bundle, out of scope for symbol analysis.

nodes.name: jspace_viz.js
nodes.summary: Step-driven (6-step) canvas visualization of J-Space: specialized brain modules, Global Workspace Theory, the hidden-intermediate-thoughts riddle, the J-Lens (Jacobian Lens) decoding internal activations, the Jacobian as a word-direction decoder, and silent/deceptive thinking. Exposes a JSpaceViz API (init/next/prev/reset) driven by the presentation engine.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE returning a module API; each step is a self-contained requestAnimationFrame draw loop on a shared dark theme; safeCanvasSetup handles DPR scaling and container guards.

nodes.name: JSpaceViz
nodes.summary: Module namespace (IIFE) holding step state, the dark THEME, animation control, the renderStep dispatcher, all six step renderers, and the public API.

nodes.name: renderStep
nodes.summary: Dispatcher that stops running animations, toggles the active [data-jstep] indicator, sets the German step caption, and calls the matching per-step renderer (0-5).

nodes.name: renderJacobian
nodes.summary: Step-4 renderer: draws an internal representation space with word-direction vectors (Spinne/acht/Netz), a rotating state vector, its projections onto each direction, and a live bar chart of what the J-Lens reads as the most likely word.

nodes.name: renderSilentThinking
nodes.summary: Step-5 renderer: illustrates 'silent thinking' with an alignment-audit scenario where the J-Lens reveals internal words (manipulation, deception, ...) that influence the action even though the model never says them.

nodes.name: knowledge.js
nodes.summary: Four-step canvas visualization of how factual knowledge ("Paris is the capital of France") is stored in a language model: the "capital-of" embedding direction, attention gathering context, FFN detector-neuron activation, and the combined picture, shown for the sentence "Die Hauptstadt von Frankreich ist ___".
nodes.languageNotes: KnowledgeViz object-literal module (this-based methods) with a step/eased-animation model; a shared drawColumn helper composes the three-column summary view.

nodes.name: KnowledgeViz
nodes.summary: Module (object literal) holding the country/capital and neuron datasets, setStep/startAnimation/render dispatch, and the four step renderers (embedding, attention, FFN, full picture).

nodes.name: renderFFN
nodes.summary: Step-2 renderer: draws an input vector, a wall of 16 detector neurons that light up for the active concepts, and the resulting shift toward the "Paris" direction.

nodes.name: kurz.html
nodes.summary: 12-line meta-refresh redirector that loads index.html in the short presentation mode (?fast=1&short=1) restricted to a curated 15-slide subset of the lndw deck.

nodes.name: neue_intro.html
nodes.summary: Self-contained animated intro page ("Was passiert da eigentlich? — Von der Sprache ins Modell"): a CSS smartphone types/speaks "warum ist der himmel blau", zooms into the screen, tokenizes the sentence, places tokens in a 2D embedding space (with a king-queen-man-woman analogy), and hands off to the Transformer. Driven by an inline beats array and keyboard/touch/click navigation.
nodes.languageNotes: Single HTML file with inline CSS and JS; a declarative beats array of state-setting functions (reverse navigation by re-setting state, CSS interpolates); also embeds an iframe to story.html at the end.

nodes.name: pe_orbit_viz.js
nodes.summary: Plotly-based step visualization of positional encodings: shows the base embedding of "Katze" and how adding a positional-encoding vector at each of 12 positions traces an orbit around it, ending with a summary connecting all position points.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE module; computes sin/cos positional encodings and renders via Plotly.react with an aggressive MutationObserver re-render on slide activation.

nodes.name: PEOrbitViz
nodes.summary: Module (IIFE) holding the word/base-embedding constants, computePE/finalVector/textPos helpers, the Plotly render pipeline, and the next/prev/reset/isOnPEOrbitSlide navigation API.

nodes.name: renderPlot
nodes.summary: Builds and plots (Plotly.react) the orbit: the grayed base embedding star, the dashed orbit circle, per-position colored dots with labels, center-to-point lines, and a final connecting line in the summary step.

nodes.name: philosophy.js
nodes.summary: Plotly visualizations for the philosophy/language slides: a SunrisePlot that fits a cosine/sinus model (-A*cos + mean + d) to the sun's elevation over 24 hours via sliders (amplitude, phase, period, vertical shift), and a lazy CooccurrencePlot horizontal bar chart of city-word co-occurrence counts.
nodes.languageNotes: Two object-literal modules; CooccurrencePlot is lazy-loaded via IntersectionObserver rather than rendered immediately.

nodes.name: SunrisePlot
nodes.summary: Module rendering the sunrise/sinus model: reads slider parameters, plots the smooth model curve over a transparent plot, and exposes showSinus/hideSinus toggles driven by fragments.

nodes.name: CooccurrencePlot
nodes.summary: Lazy module rendering a horizontal bar chart of word co-occurrence counts (e.g. Hamburg+Elbe vs Hamburg+Donau) to motivate why word association is a statistical signal.

nodes.name: plotly.min.js
nodes.summary: Bundled/minified Plotly.js v2.35.0 (MIT) providing the global Plotly plotting library (newPlot/react/relayout) used by the lndw demo visualizations.
nodes.languageNotes: Third-party UMD bundle, out of scope for symbol analysis.

nodes.name: presentation.js
nodes.summary: The lndw slide-deck engine: a DemoRegistry that declaratively wires per-slide interactive demos (next/prev/guards/lifecycle), a FragmentActions map, a typewriter code-reveal effect, the core Presentation controller (slides, fragments, ?slides=/?fast=/?short=/#N URL selection, overview + search, fullscreen), a per-slide Selection panel with a 3x-Esc URL builder, an InputHandler (keyboard/touch/wheel), a LoadingStatus/LoadingTasks boot pipeline, and a runBootSequence that renders TeX math slide-by-slide via temml and drains heavy plot/demo tasks.
nodes.languageNotes: Many IIFE/object modules cooperating through globals; wraps Plotly newPlot/react to feed the loading spinner, and monkey-patches nothing else; math is rendered with temml.renderToString.

nodes.name: DemoRegistry
nodes.summary: Declarative registry of the deck's interactive demos (NNStepDemo, TrainingViz, JSpaceViz, PEOrbitViz, ResidualNotebook, etc.) with per-demo guards, slide tests, and onEnter/onLeave hooks; exposes tryNavigate and notifyEnter so navigation is consumed by an active demo before falling back to slide changes.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.summary: Core deck controller: initializes the slide list from ?slides= (indexes/ranges/IDs), handles ?fast=/?short= reordering, steps through fragments (executing FragmentActions), manages the overview grid with type-to-filter search, fullscreen, and the progress UI.

nodes.name: Selection
nodes.summary: Per-slide checkbox selection panel that edits the ?slides= URL live (writing slide IDs), with a 3x-Esc open/close trigger, a copy/preview/clear panel, and URL normalization.

nodes.name: InputHandler
nodes.summary: Global input handler binding keyboard (arrows/space/digits/special keys), touch swipe, and mouse-wheel (with cooldown) to deck navigation, routing through DemoRegistry before Presentation.

nodes.name: runBootSequence
nodes.summary: Async boot pipeline that renders math (temml) slide by slide with per-slide loading status, drains the LoadingTasks queue of heavy plot/demo steps, runs optional intuition/attention init, then reveals the page.

nodes.name: residual_stream_notebook.js
nodes.summary: Animated visualization of the transformer residual stream as a notebook: five layers of 'experts' progressively scribble annotations (underlines, brackets, arrows, scribbles, boxes, margin notes) onto the sentence "Die Katze saß auf der Matte weil sie müde war", each layer adding a deeper linguistic/semantic reading.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE module with heavy layout guardrails: per-character Range rect measurement, transform-scale correction, line-break segmentation, a per-annotation rAF retry loop, a verifyCount self-repair guardrail, and ResizeObserver/font-ready reflow.

nodes.name: ResidualNotebook
nodes.summary: Module (IIFE) holding the five layer definitions, the notebook render, nextLayer/prevLayer stepping, the annotation builder/render with guardrails, and the isOnNotebookSlide/canGoNext/canGoPrev API used by the presentation engine.

nodes.name: buildAnnotationEls
nodes.summary: Builds the DOM/SVG elements for a single annotation (underline, highlight, circle, bracket, strikethrough, box, arrow, margin-note, scribble, checkmark), positioned from measured character rects; returns null when the text is not yet measurable.

nodes.name: sheaves_presentation.js
nodes.summary: A ~2670-line standalone slide deck + visualization engine teaching sheaves/cohomology/topos/HoTT: an Assets loader, a minimal Presentation controller with math rendering (temml), and a vizRegistry of ~15 canvas/Plotly visualizations (panorama, sheaf 3D, stalks, bird, topology, cohomology, Cech, laser, fiber bundle, gauge/parallel transport, calibration/Homotopy, infinity-sheaf/Manhattan, fibration, Hopf fibration, topoi, HoTT).
nodes.languageNotes: Separate Presentation global from the main deck; vizRegistry maps container IDs to draw functions; 3D plots (sheaf-3d, hopf) use Plotly, the rest use canvas 2D with requestAnimationFrame.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.summary: Minimal slide engine for the sheaves deck: inits slides, renders math (temml.renderToString), steps through fragments, and triggers the per-slide visualizations via initSlideViz after assets load.

nodes.name: initSlideViz
nodes.summary: Cancels running viz animations, then for the active slide invokes each registered vizRegistry function against its .viz-container to (re)start that slide's visualization.

nodes.name: Assets
nodes.summary: Robust asset loader (images + audio) used by the bird/Manhattan visualizations; resolves to null and logs a German fallback warning when a file is missing.

nodes.name: temml.min.js
nodes.summary: Bundled/minified temml (a KaTeX-derived, TypeScript-friendly TeX typesetting library) providing temml.renderToString used to render math in the presentation decks.
nodes.languageNotes: Third-party minified bundle, out of scope for symbol analysis.

nodes.name: trace_through_loss_landscape.js
nodes.summary: Singleton 3D loss-landscape plotter (Plotly) for single-neuron, single-input linear models: reads the live model weights and dataset globals, computes an MSE surface over (w,b), and animates the optimization path and current position, preserving the camera and deferring updates while the user interacts.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE singleton with _state; theme switching via global is_dark_mode; Plotly.newPlot on first render then Plotly.react with saved camera; lazy CDN fallback for Plotly.

nodes.name: LossLandscape
nodes.summary: Module (IIFE singleton) holding all state and the public init_loss_landscape/stop/update/destroy API; orchestrates data sync, loss/surface computation, camera preservation, interaction deferral, and the 800ms render tick.

nodes.name: _renderPlot
nodes.summary: Builds the surface trace plus optimization-path and current-position 3D traces, applies the theme layout with preserved camera, and either newPlot (first time) or react (diff update), skipping render when the plot hash is unchanged.

nodes.name: training_demo.js
nodes.summary: IIFE exposing window.TrainingDemo that trains a small 4-4-2 feedforward network in-browser on six cat/dog photos, animating the forward pass, backpropagation, and SGD weight updates on a canvas beside a 3D loss-landscape view in Plotly.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE with a single mutable state object `s`; no external imports; canvas 2D plus Plotly; German UI strings.

nodes.name: fwd
nodes.summary: Runs the forward pass of the 4-4-2 net (ReLU hidden layer, softmax output with a 0.5 display temperature) and stores inputs, hidden activations, logits, and outputs in state.

nodes.name: bwd
nodes.summary: Computes cross-entropy loss and backpropagates gradients to the output and hidden layers, using a 0.01 slope for dead ReLU units.

nodes.name: upd
nodes.summary: Applies an SGD step to W1, b1, W2, and b2 at the given learning rate, snapshotting the previous weights so the update animation can show deltas.

nodes.name: extractFeatures
nodes.summary: Downsamples a loaded image to 2x2 on an offscreen canvas and returns four normalized luminance values used as the network's input features.

nodes.name: computeFixedSurface
nodes.summary: Precomputes a 45x45 grid of the real network loss over two swept weights (all others frozen at their initial values) to build a static 3D loss landscape.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Renders the full canvas scene: input image, network layers and connections with forward-flow and gradient highlighting, trace dots, output bars, loss readout, and a loss sparkline.

nodes.name: updatePlot
nodes.summary: Builds and updates the Plotly 3D loss-surface plot with the current weight ball and a trailing path, using restyle on subsequent frames to keep the camera and surface stable.

nodes.name: tick
nodes.summary: requestAnimationFrame main loop driving the phase state machine (forward, loss, backprop, update, next image) and recording loss and weight-position history.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Public entry point that sizes the canvas, initializes weights, preloads the images, computes the fixed loss surface, and draws the first frame.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the animation loop plus a periodic timer that refreshes the 3D plot only while the Training slide is active.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the requestAnimationFrame loop and clears the plot-update timer.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Stops and reinitializes the network, fixed loss surface, and loss/position histories to a clean starting state.

nodes.name: training_viz.js
nodes.summary: Global TrainingViz object implementing a simple step-through 'Training' slide that simulates a language model predicting the next word, showing correct/wrong prediction cards and a Plotly loss chart.
nodes.languageNotes: Object literal of methods with German UI strings; simulates model improvement by raising correctProb with each step; uses an IntersectionObserver to defer chart rendering until the container is visible.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the sentence with the target word highlighted, the correct/wrong prediction cards, and the loss display for the current position.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Advances one step by simulating a model prediction whose correctness improves over time, records loss/correctness history, and advances the word index (advancing slides when all examples are done).

nodes.name: renderChart
nodes.summary: Renders a Plotly marker-and-line loss chart colored by correctness, sized to its container.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Renders the initial state and sets up an IntersectionObserver to (re)render the chart once the plot container becomes visible.

nodes.name: training.html
nodes.summary: Standalone draft presentation page hosting the 'Training' slide: a network canvas, a 3D loss-landscape container, a nav bar, and inline wiring that boots TrainingDemo through the LoadingTasks pipeline.
nodes.languageNotes: Loads vendor scripts (jquery/plotly/temml) plus presentation.js and training_demo.js; inline fitSlides() scales slide content to the viewport.

nodes.name: zipf_data.json
nodes.summary: Precomputed word-frequency data (total/unique word counts and top-word frequency lists) for Finnegans Wake and the King James Bible, consumed by zipf.js to demonstrate Zipf's law.

nodes.name: zipf.js
nodes.summary: Global ZipfViz object that fetches real word-frequency data and plots Zipf's law (rank vs. frequency, log-log) for Finnegans Wake and the King James Bible with word annotations.
nodes.languageNotes: Object literal of methods; async fetch with a graceful empty fallback; log-log Plotly layout with hand-placed annotations.

nodes.name: loadData
nodes.summary: Fetches and caches zipf_data.json (with a graceful empty-object fallback) and returns the {finwake, kjv} frequency datasets.

nodes.name: buildTrace
nodes.summary: Builds a Plotly markers-and-lines trace for a dataset's top frequencies with per-point hover text showing rank, word, and count.

nodes.name: buildAnnotations
nodes.summary: Builds Plotly annotations labeling the top-8 words, mid-list ellipsis markers, and the last top-N word with its frequency.

nodes.name: renderGermanZipf
nodes.summary: Assembles the log-log Zipf plot comparing the two corpora (top 200 words) with combined annotations and a fitted y-range, then renders it via Plotly.react.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Entry point that triggers renderGermanZipf to build the Zipf plot.

nodes.name: backprop_slides.js
nodes.summary: Canvas/SVG/Plotly visualizations for the Backpropagation and ResNet slides of the AI-history deck, wrapped in the BPSlides IIFE module. Covers forward/backward flow animation, chain rule, gradient descent, 3D loss landscape, vanishing gradients, ResNet diagrams, and TeML math rendering.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE module exposing a large public API; per-slide init triggered by a MutationObserver watching the active slide's data-title.

nodes.name: BPSlides
nodes.summary: The BPSlides module object (IIFE) exposing the public API of all backprop/ResNet slide visualizations, including init helpers and interactive controls wired to inline onclick/oninput handlers.

nodes.name: initAll
nodes.summary: Orchestrates initialization of all backprop slide widgets (forward viz, activations, flow, chain, gradient descent, vanishing, ResNet, loss landscape, timeline) after renderTemml runs.

nodes.name: initLossLandscape
nodes.summary: Renders an interactive 3D loss landscape on canvas with a draggable/zoomable camera and an animated ball performing gradient descent with momentum, plus respawn/pause/speed controls.

nodes.name: initFlowAnimation
nodes.summary: Sets up the forward/backward pass canvas diagram and stores drawBase/drawSignal callbacks used to animate a glowing signal travelling across network layers toward or away from the loss.

nodes.name: drawChainViz
nodes.summary: Draws the chain-rule product of per-layer local derivatives on canvas, color-coding each layer and flagging vanishing gradients when the product collapses.

nodes.name: drawGDViz
nodes.summary: Plots the 1D loss curve, the current weight position, the gradient arrow scaled by the learning rate, and the descent history trail for the gradient-descent slide.

nodes.name: updateVanishViz
nodes.summary: Renders a bar chart of gradient strength decaying across network depth, driven by depth and per-layer factor sliders, to illustrate the vanishing gradient problem.

nodes.name: initResnetConcept
nodes.summary: Builds an inline SVG diagram of a residual block (x -> F(x) -> + -> F(x)+x) with the identity shortcut path to explain ResNets.

nodes.name: initResnetArchDiagram
nodes.summary: Renders an SVG architecture diagram of a full ResNet residual block (Conv, BN+ReLU, Conv, F(x)+x, ReLU) with the skip connection arc.

nodes.name: initNNTimeline
nodes.summary: Creates a Plotly scatter timeline of neural-network milestones from McCulloch-Pitts (1943) through ResNet and the Transformer to ChatGPT (2022).

nodes.name: renderTemml
nodes.summary: Renders TeML math in both display (data-temml) elements and inline $...$ spans found via a TreeWalker, replacing matched text with rendered output.

nodes.name: initForwardViz
nodes.summary: Generates an SVG neural-network diagram (input/hidden/output layers with full connections and W*x+b -> sigma labels) for the backprop overview slide.

nodes.name: initActivationViz
nodes.summary: Draws small canvas plots of the ReLU, sigmoid, and tanh activation functions with axes for the activation-function slide.

nodes.name: history_presentation.js
nodes.summary: Minimal slide-deck presentation engine (adapted from presentation.js) that drives slide navigation, fragments, an overview grid, fullscreen, and keyboard/touch controls for the AI-history deck, and triggers viz re-rendering on slide change.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE module (Presentation) plus top-level keydown/touch listeners and a fitSlides autoscaler; calls HistoryViz.init() from history.js.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.summary: The presentation engine object exposing init, next, prev, goTo, toggleOverview, toggleFullscreen, and closeOverview to navigate the slide deck and sync the progress bar, counter, and overview thumbnails.

nodes.name: fitSlides

nodes.name: custom.py
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled reverse-mode autodiff: a Var computational-graph node whose arithmetic ops (+, *, sin) each record a per-node _backward gradient closure, and backward() topologically sorts the graph then runs the closures to accumulate gradients.
nodes.languageNotes: Each op stores a Python closure (_backward) as its gradient rule; backward() seeds the output's adjoint to 1.0 and traverses a reverse topological order — the minimal tensor-core of a deep-learning framework.

nodes.name: Var
nodes.summary: A node in the computational graph holding a value, an accumulated gradient (adjoint), its children, and a _backward closure; the + and * operators plus sin() build child nodes and attach the corresponding gradient-propagation closures.

nodes.name: backward
nodes.summary: Driver of reverse-mode autodiff: recursively builds a topological order of the graph, seeds the output's gradient to 1.0, then runs each node's _backward closure in reverse to accumulate df/dx for all leaf inputs.

nodes.name: Library.v
nodes.summary: Foundational Coq library for the coherent-world-models chapter. Defines the basic types (SubjectMatter, Region, Codomain, Trace, AccessFunction, ViewTranslation, Context, ContextRefinement), the admissible-transition class T (TransitionKind, AdmissibleTransition), the hierarchy of sameness predicates (equality, isomorphism, homotopy, approximation, statistical, model-theoretic), and indexicality. Every other file in the directory imports it.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines the shared vocabulary; uses Notation aliases (W, R, Region, Trace) and two proven weakening lemmas (eq_to_iso, iso_to_homotopy).

nodes.name: SubjectMatter
nodes.summary: The type W with internal structure; the thing the whole framework represents without being identical to.

nodes.name: AccessFunction
nodes.summary: An observation arrow O: W -> R mapping a region of the subject matter to a trace in a codomain.

nodes.name: ViewTranslation
nodes.summary: A map between two codomains (a view-to-view translation), the carrier of one class of admissible transition.

nodes.name: TransitionKind
nodes.summary: Inductive sum of the three kinds of transition: observation, translation, and context refinement.

nodes.name: AdmissibleTransition
nodes.summary: The predicate marking a TransitionKind as licensed (belonging to the class T), the chapter's central licence machinery.

nodes.name: Iso
nodes.summary: An isomorphism as an invertible pair of maps with both round-trip equalities; the witness for isomorphism-sameness.

nodes.name: HomotopyEquiv
nodes.summary: A homotopy equivalence modelled as mutually inverse maps up to pointwise equality; the witness for homotopy-sameness.

nodes.name: CommonModel
nodes.summary: A single Model satisfying every theory in a list; the witness for model-theoretic sameness.

nodes.name: IndexicalTrace
nodes.summary: A trace that points beyond itself to a possible source, capturing indexicality as data rather than a given.

nodes.name: eq_to_iso
nodes.summary: Proves equality weakens to isomorphism by exhibiting the identity isomorphism on a type.

nodes.name: iso_to_homotopy
nodes.summary: Proves isomorphism weakens to homotopy equivalence by reusing the isomorphism's forward/backward maps.

nodes.name: Traces.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes what an access function leaves behind: a ProducedTrace bundling the access function, region, and image proof, plus the four trace properties (transformed, mediated, underdetermined, possibly indexical) and the inference task of recovering a (source, access) pair from a trace.
nodes.languageNotes: Works around Coq 8.20's strict dependent-projection handling with explicit-parameter projection definitions (PTAccess, PTRegion, PTTrace).

nodes.name: ProducedTrace
nodes.summary: A trace paired with its producing access function and region, with an equality witness that the trace is the image of the region.

nodes.name: MediatedSetup
nodes.summary: Two access functions on the same source/codomain witnessing that a trace carries the marks of its procedure.

nodes.name: Inference
nodes.summary: The (partial) recovery of one possible (source, access) pair from a given trace, modelled via PossibleSource.

nodes.name: Transformed
nodes.summary: Predicate stating a trace is the output of some access function applied to a region of a subject matter.

nodes.name: Underdetermined
nodes.summary: Predicate stating that at least two distinct (source, access) pairs can yield the same trace, so neither is determined by the trace alone.

nodes.name: make_example
nodes.summary: Constructs a TraceExample from a subject matter, codomain, access function, and source/target equalities; unifies the chapter's four concrete trace examples.

nodes.name: inferences_disagree
nodes.summary: Predicate that two inferences from the same trace disagree (different region or different access), formalizing non-unique inference.

nodes.name: Commitments.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes the chapter's five foundational commitments (indirect realism, internal structure, existence of admissible transitions, coherence-necessary-not-sufficient, correspondence-separate) plus the wordless-introspection limit case, Kant's thing-in-itself, and the unresolved dispute with qualia-primary views.

nodes.name: IndirectRealism
nodes.summary: A subject matter kept separate from its codomain, witnessing that a trace lives in the codomain r, never in the source s.

nodes.name: AdmissibleClass
nodes.summary: Witnesses a non-trivial class T by exhibiting at least one licensed observation, translation, and refinement.

nodes.name: Position
nodes.summary: Inductive type marking which default (indirect realism vs qualia-primary) a view takes in the foundational dispute.

nodes.name: our_position
nodes.summary: Declares the chapter's default stance to be IndirectRealismDefault, i.e. the mediated, communicable case.

nodes.name: ThreeDifferences.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes the three independent sources of disagreement between a subject matter and a trace: world-level, channel-level (calibrable), and processing-level, with a diagnostic disjunction (DisagreementKind) and the discipline to locate the difference at the right level.

nodes.name: WorldDifference
nodes.summary: Two subject matters that genuinely differ (no identification procedure), the world-level source of disagreement.

nodes.name: ChannelDifference
nodes.summary: Two instruments reading the same subject matter differently; the channel-level source addressed by calibration.

nodes.name: ProcessingDifference
nodes.summary: Two interpretations of the same trace yielding different conclusions; the processing-level source of disagreement.

nodes.name: DisagreementKind
nodes.summary: Inductive diagnostic naming where a disagreement lives: world, channel, processing, or not-yet-tellable.

nodes.name: locate_difference
nodes.summary: Placeholder for the boxed discipline to ask which level is responsible for a given disagreement.

nodes.name: NotionsOfSameness.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes the chapter's six-row hierarchy of sameness (literal, isomorphism, homotopy, approximation, statistical, model-theoretic) as a weakening tower of lemmas, the forbidden silent-upgrade category error, the transformation triangle, and parallel examples across sense data, measurement, and mathematics.

nodes.name: hierarchy_implications
nodes.summary: Conjunction stating each row of the sameness hierarchy implies the next weaker row, from equality down to model-theoretic compatibility.

nodes.name: eq_to_iso_witness
nodes.summary: Proves literal sameness weakens to isomorphism by exhibiting the identity isomorphism.

nodes.name: iso_to_homotopy_witness
nodes.summary: Proves isomorphism-sameness weakens to homotopy-sameness by reusing the invertible map.

nodes.name: approx_is_not_eq
nodes.summary: States that an approximate reading is not literal equality, the concrete form of the forbidden approximation-as-equality error.

nodes.name: SilentUpgradeError
nodes.summary: Inductive type naming the standing category errors: treating approximation as equality, isomorphism as identity, statistical agreement as proof, consistency as truth.

nodes.name: TransformationTriangle
nodes.summary: Two representations meeting at a common target via two transitions, the structure that replaces the naive R_A = R_B? question.

nodes.name: AdmissibleTransitions.v
nodes.summary: Builds the higher-level structure over the class T: InT as the disjunction of licensed observation/translation/refinement, T's three simultaneous interpretations (subcategory constraint, Bayesian prior, Occam penalty), six kinds of admissible transition, and the Sellarsian web as the alternative to foundationalism.

nodes.name: InT
nodes.summary: The disjunction predicate that a transition kind is a licensed member of T (observation, translation, or refinement).

nodes.name: SellarsianWeb
nodes.summary: A web of four representations joined by licensed bidirectional transitions, embodying the self-correcting enterprise with no foundational top.

nodes.name: web_is_licensed
nodes.summary: Placeholder asserting that every arrow in a SellarsianWeb has been independently justified.

nodes.name: ContextsAndSites.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes contexts (tuples of six facets: where, when, who, how, terms, tradition), refinements as context morphisms, covers and admissible covers, Grothendieck topologies, sites, and contravariant representation schemes (presheaves) into a target category.

nodes.name: Cover
nodes.summary: A family of sub-contexts with inclusion maps whose images together capture everything relevant about a context.

nodes.name: GrothendieckTopology
nodes.summary: A cover rule on a context category closed under pullback and composition, the axioms that define a Grothendieck topology.

nodes.name: Site
nodes.summary: A context category equipped with a Grothendieck topology, the domain on which presheaves and sheaves live.

nodes.name: RepresentationScheme
nodes.summary: A contravariant assignment from contexts to sections in a target category, the general form of a presheaf.

nodes.name: cover_condition
nodes.summary: Placeholder stating that the union of a cover's patch images equals the whole context.

nodes.name: Sheaves.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes presheaves and the sheaf condition (compatible local data on an admissible cover implies unique global data), its pullback form for two patches, the three regimes (strict, homotopical, empirical), and the running train-at-a-platform example with five channels plus the group-presentations parallel.

nodes.name: Presheaf
nodes.summary: A contravariant functor from contexts to types assigning a set of local sections to every context.

nodes.name: sheaf_condition
nodes.summary: The sheaf condition as a Prop: compatible local sections over an admissible cover force a unique global section (existence and uniqueness, here as a placeholder).

nodes.name: sheaf_pullback
nodes.summary: The two-patch form of the sheaf condition, stating F(c) is the pullback of F(c_1) and F(c_2) over the overlap.

nodes.name: SheafRegime
nodes.summary: Inductive naming the three regimes in which the sheaf condition runs: strict, homotopical, and empirical.

nodes.name: TrainCover
nodes.summary: The running example's admissible cover of a train event by five channels (visual, auditory, radar, linguistic, archival).

nodes.name: EqualizersAndPullbacks.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes equalizers (where two parallel maps agree) and pullbacks (agreement through a shared target) as categorical limits with universal properties, their set-level forms, homotopical equalizers, and worked examples (two thermometers, two proofs, two tracks, two definitions of prime).

nodes.name: Equalizer
nodes.summary: The equalizer of two parallel maps: a carrier of points of agreement with the universal property.

nodes.name: PullbackGeneral
nodes.summary: The pullback of two maps to a common target: pairs (x, y) with f(x) = g(y), with the universal property.

nodes.name: set_equalizer
nodes.summary: The explicit set-level equalizer {x in X | f x = g x}, the naive form of the categorical equalizer.

nodes.name: set_pullback
nodes.summary: The explicit set-level pullback {(x, y) | f x = g y}, the naive form of the categorical pullback.

nodes.name: HigherCoherence.v
nodes.summary: Introduces higher-categorical structure: strict vs homotopical coherence, the recursive tower of n-cells (0-cells through 3-cells), the Cech nerve of a cover, infinity-sheaves valued in infinity-groupoids, and worked examples (lightning-and-thunder, equivalent categories).

nodes.name: StrictCoherence
nodes.summary: The strict regime where two routes A->C (direct vs via B) agree on the nose.

nodes.name: TwoMorphism
nodes.summary: A 2-cell witnessing that two routes are not equal but homotopically deformable into each other.

nodes.name: CechNerve
nodes.summary: The simplicial object of a cover: patches in degree 0, pairwise overlaps in degree 1, triple overlaps in degree 2, with face and degeneracy maps.

nodes.name: InfinitySheaf
nodes.summary: A sheaf-like object valued in infinity-groupoids over the Cech nerve, with a locality condition.

nodes.name: infinity_sheaf_condition
nodes.summary: Placeholder for the sheaf condition in infinity-groupoids: the limit over the Cech nerve reproduces the global sections.

nodes.name: ObserverInDiagram.v
nodes.summary: Puts the inquirer back in the diagram: models every access to a subject matter as a six-stage pipeline (subject, signal, internal representation, report, model) with domain examples (vision, audition, mathematics, history) and the discipline that every claim must be backed by a licensed transition.

nodes.name: ObserverPipeline
nodes.summary: The composite access pipeline from subject matter to model via stimulus pickup, neural processing, encoding, and calibration.

nodes.name: BackedClaim
nodes.summary: A claim about the subject matter that is backed by an admissible transition preserving the structure invoked.

nodes.name: observer_composite
nodes.summary: Composes the four pipeline stages into a single function from subject matter to model.

nodes.name: claim_is_backed
nodes.summary: Predicate that a claim about the subject matter is licensed by a transition preserving the invoked structure.

nodes.name: MasterDiagram.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes where AI enters: parametric maps and neural-network morphisms (Transformer residual update, multi-head attention, embeddings, multimodal alignment), training and generative models, hallucination as internal coherence without grounded descent, the master diagram W -> R_i -> G with its five settings, and the sameness hierarchy in the descent context.

nodes.name: MasterDiagram
nodes.summary: The master shape W -> R_i -> G: a subject matter, a family of representations, observation arrows, admissible transitions, and a global section, with source/target coherence constraints.

nodes.name: MultiHeadAttention
nodes.summary: Multi-head attention Attn(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k)) V, expressed as a record of scores and their softmax aggregation.

nodes.name: TransformerLayer
nodes.summary: A residual Transformer layer H_{l+1} = H_l + F(H_l), capturing the learnable update over a hidden state.

nodes.name: Hallucination
nodes.summary: A model section that is internally self-consistent yet not grounded in the world it is supposed to represent.

nodes.name: global_section_exists
nodes.summary: Placeholder asserting a global section exists for a master diagram, concretely the sheaf condition over all views.

nodes.name: Ologs.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes ologs (Spivak & Kent ontology logs): types as labelled kinds-of-thing, arrows as functional relations, commutativity asserted via explicit equalities, the calibrated-thermometer worked example, and the master diagram recast as an olog.

nodes.name: OlogArrow
nodes.summary: A functional relation between two olog types carrying a verb-phrase label; every source entity maps to exactly one target.

nodes.name: CommutativeSquare
nodes.summary: An explicitly commuting square of olog arrows, with the commutativity equality supplied externally.

nodes.name: ThermometerOlog
nodes.summary: The thermometer example as two routes from thermometer to temperature, whose agreement witnesses calibration (or whose failure marks a hole).

nodes.name: MasterOlog
nodes.summary: The master diagram W -> R -> G recast as an olog with an observation arrow and a gluing arrow.

nodes.name: master_descent
nodes.summary: The (degenerate, trivially holding) descent/commutativity condition for the master olog; the real sheaf condition lives in Sheaves.v.

nodes.name: Forbidden.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes the chapter's five forbidden moves: silent upgrade of a weaker sameness, an unconstrained T (vacuous coherence), identifying G with W, mistaking internal coherence for descent, and treating a borrowed analogy as a theorem, closing with a useful analogy is not a theorem.

nodes.name: SilentUpgrade
nodes.summary: An unjustified implication from a weaker sameness claim to a stronger one, without carrying the residual.

nodes.name: UnconstrainedT
nodes.summary: A T in which every arrow is licensed, making coherence vacuous because every family of local sections agrees.

nodes.name: BorrowedAnalogy
nodes.summary: A structural analogy between two categories being used as a theorem in the borrowed category.

nodes.name: analogy_not_theorem_boxed
nodes.summary: The boxed principle that a useful analogy is not a theorem, stated as a Prop over borrowed analogies.

nodes.name: PracticalProcedure.v
nodes.summary: Compresses the whole framework into a nine-step procedure (raw datum, interpretation, chain, overlaps, licences, sameness choice, global model, residuals, next observation) as a sequence of records, closing with the principle that anomalies are constraints not yet integrated, not defeats.

nodes.name: Procedure
nodes.summary: The full nine-step procedure packaged as a single record bundling all steps in order.

nodes.name: Step5_Licences
nodes.summary: Step 5 of the procedure: the list of licensed transitions, each a member of T.

nodes.name: SamenessChoice
nodes.summary: Step 6 of the procedure: which sameness level (literal, isomorphism, homotopy, approximation, statistical, model-theoretic) the comparison uses.

nodes.name: Tarski.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes Tarski's Convention T (object-language, meta-language, quotation-name, proposition, and the iff), truth as an interface condition, the coherence tradition, the synthesis of coherence plus correspondence, the completed diagram, three pathologies, Tarski's four-discipline, the six-step audit protocol, and the closing synthesis.

nodes.name: ConventionT
nodes.summary: Tarski's Convention T: an object-sentence is true in L iff the meta-language proposition p, a meta-level biconditional relating truth-values.

nodes.name: CoherenceAndCorrespondence
nodes.summary: The synthesis requiring both descent on every admissible cover and Tarski at every contact point, jointly, for truth.

nodes.name: CompletedDiagram
nodes.summary: The master diagram with three sorts of arrows, each carrying its own condition: licence on O_i, coherence on T_i, Tarski on G->W.

nodes.name: ClosingSynthesis
nodes.summary: The closing synthesis: truth from coherence plus correspondence, with the residual recorded rather than hidden.

nodes.name: AILLM.v
nodes.summary: Applies the framework to LLMs: the LLM in the master diagram, internal descent techniques (in-context learning, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, verifier-guided search), the lack of grounded observation and its mitigations (RAG, tools, formal verification), a refined hallucination diagnosis, training dynamics, the framework's limits, and an honest closing.

nodes.name: LLMSetup
nodes.summary: An LLM as a system: subject matter, corpus, representations, the sampling step (W -> R), the trained model, and the internal fit (R -> G).

nodes.name: HallucinationDiagnosis
nodes.summary: Inductive naming the four LLM failure modes: non-glueable presheaf, self-consistent fantasy, factbook, and calibrated error.

nodes.name: NonGlueablePresheaf
nodes.summary: A hallucination as a non-glueable presheaf: local sections exist but the sheaf condition fails and correspondence also fails.

nodes.name: AugmentedLLM
nodes.summary: An LLM augmented with admissible transitions (RAG, tools, formal verification, RLHF) to add grounded contact.

nodes.name: TrainingDynamics
nodes.summary: The training chain D -> B -> L -> grad -> theta, with sampling, forward, backward, and SGD steps composing to one gradient-descent step.

nodes.name: FrameworkLimit
nodes.summary: Inductive naming the framework's limits: emergent capabilities, in-context learning as a meta-phenomenon, training dynamics, and value alignment.

nodes.name: hallucination_table
nodes.summary: The chapter's diagnosis table mapping each hallucination mode to what is broken and the typical remedy (an empty list placeholder here).

nodes.name: ThreePathologies.v
nodes.summary: Formalizes the three failure modes, each breaking exactly one of coherence or correspondence: self-consistent fantasy (breaks correspondence), contact-point junkie (breaks coherence), and contact-point liar (a hallucinating model), with their break-points on the diagram and remedies.

nodes.name: SelfConsistentFantasy
nodes.summary: A perfectly coherent fiction: descent holds and all arrows are licensed, but Tarski fails at the contact points, breaking correspondence.

nodes.name: ContactPointJunkie
nodes.summary: A factbook: every claim individually true at its contact point, but descent never delivers a coherent global model, breaking coherence.

nodes.name: PathologyDiagnosis
nodes.summary: Inductive naming the three pathologies for a unified diagnosis, each paired with a distinct remedy.

nodes.name: SCF_failure_mode
nodes.summary: Declares that the self-consistent fantasy breaks the correspondence condition.

nodes.name: CPJ_failure_mode
nodes.summary: Declares that the contact-point junkie breaks the coherence condition.

nodes.name: TheoryChain.v
nodes.summary: Lays out the nine-stage chain of refinements (distinction to invariance), maps each theory (sets/type theory, categories, topology, sheaves, higher categories, model theory, probability, ML) to the stages it serves, situates the position relative to structural realism, and states the one-sentence world-model thesis with provisional globality.

nodes.name: ChainStage
nodes.summary: Inductive naming the nine stages of the refinement chain, from distinction (sets) to invariance (what survives T).

nodes.name: WorldModelDefinition
nodes.summary: The one-sentence thesis: a world model is the global section recovered from local descent data along an admissible cover, provisionally, revisably, and never identical to the subject matter.

nodes.name: next_stage
nodes.summary: Maps each chain stage to the next refinement in the nine-stage chain (None at the last stage).

nodes.name: stage_position
nodes.summary: Assigns a numeric position 0-8 to each stage of the chain.

nodes.name: all_contributions
nodes.summary: The list of every theory's contribution to the chain stages, per the chapter's table.

nodes.summary: Static JS linter for the blog: a hand-rolled tokenizer plus a battery of regex checks (bracket balance, unclosed strings/comments, debugger, duplicate declarations, DOM API typos, implied globals) with rich-formatted error/warning/info severity reporting.
