nodes.name: tokenize_js
nodes.summary: Character-by-character JS tokenizer yielding (type, value, line) for code, strings, template literals, comments, and regex literals; the foundation that keeps every other checker from false-positiving inside literals.

nodes.name: check_bracket_balance
nodes.summary: Stack-based check for mismatched, unexpected, and unclosed (), {}, [] pairs over the code-only output of the tokenizer.

nodes.name: check_common_mistakes
nodes.summary: Pattern table of ~60 common JavaScript typos and case errors (getElementByID, innerHtml, JSON.Stringify, docuemnt, setTimout, …) flagged line by line.

nodes.name: check_implied_globals
nodes.summary: Heuristic that collects declared variables (var/let/const, parameters, destructuring, loops) and known browser/Node globals to detect accidental assignments to undeclared globals.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: resolves mixed file/folder/glob inputs, runs all checkers with a progress bar, renders per-file issue trees and a summary table, and exits 1 only on critical errors.

nodes.name: keypoint_test.js
nodes.summary: Node smoke test for keypoint.js that builds .md > blockquote trees on a small DOM stub and verifies classifyBlockquote/upgradeBlockquote/upgradeBlockquotes promote short statements and attributed quotes into .kp-block cards while skipping long, complex, formal, or already-tagged ones.
nodes.languageNotes: The DOM stub makes firstChild a read-only getter to mirror real DOM semantics, which keypoint.js relies on.

nodes.name: latex_error_checker.py
nodes.summary: Playwright-based scanner that starts a PHP built-in server, opens every lesson in headless Chromium, and fails on console errors, JS exceptions, network failures, and KaTeX/Temml/MathJax parse errors in the rendered DOM, plus a source-level phase flagging risky LaTeX patterns.
nodes.languageNotes: Auto-installs Playwright Chromium, supports parallel page scanning via a pool of browser contexts, and can save per-page Playwright traces for failed pages.

nodes.name: scan_page_with_browser
nodes.summary: Navigates one page, waits for math rendering to settle, and captures console errors/warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, .katex-error/.temml-error/.mjx-error DOM elements, and regex-detected LaTeX leaks.

nodes.name: scan_html_for_latex_errors
nodes.summary: Runs a set of KaTeX/Temml/MathJax ParseError regexes over fully-rendered HTML and returns deduplicated, entity-decoded issues with approximate line numbers.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI driver: discovers .php/.js files, runs the browser phase (with optional PHP server) and the source phase, prints rich results, and exits 1 on any rendered failure.

nodes.name: lesson_guard.py
nodes.summary: Browser-free static regression guard for the Math IV lesson (math_iv.php + math_iv_affine.js): checks markdown headings sit inside .md divs, citation keys exist in literature.js, auto-rotate is off, 3D canvases are wired to bind3DNav/drawAxes3D, fold matrices stay symbolic, and the quad loop destructures (u, v).
nodes.languageNotes: Each guard encodes a concrete past bug (G1–G7 in the docstring); LESSONS is an extendable (php, js) pair list.

nodes.name: guard_headings_in_md
nodes.summary: Walks the PHP template with a div-open stack to ensure every markdown heading is inside a <div class="…md…"> block, since headings outside one neither render nor appear in the TOC.

nodes.name: guard_citation_keys
nodes.summary: Extracts every \cite/\footcite key used in the lesson and fails for any key not defined in literature.js, preventing broken bibtexify() rendering.

nodes.name: link_checker.py
nodes.summary: Validates every URL in literature.js by fetching it with browser-like HTTP/2 headers; passes on 2xx (plus %PDF magic check for .pdf links), classifies bot protection and SSL quirks as soft passes, and retries transient 5xx/429 once.
nodes.languageNotes: Two-pass regex parser for literature.js entries (order of title:/url: fields doesn't matter); concurrent checking via ThreadPoolExecutor over strict and relaxed httpx clients.

nodes.name: Outcome
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing the result of one URL check: category (ok/soft_pass/fail), HTTP status, server/via headers, cookies, body snippet, and reason, with ok/is_real_fail/is_ssl_error/shorten_reason helpers.

nodes.name: parse_literature_file
nodes.summary: Two-pass line parser that yields (key, title, url) for every entry in literature.js that carries a url: field.

nodes.name: check_url
nodes.summary: Multi-strategy check for a single URL: strict-SSL fetch, SSL-bypass retry on TLS errors, bot-protection detection on 401/403, and one retry after a delay for transient statuses.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: resolves literature.js, groups entries by URL, checks them concurrently with a progress bar, prints failures/soft-passes/malformed sections plus a summary table, and exits 1 on real failures.

nodes.name: math_alt_test.js
nodes.summary: Node smoke test for the math-alternative-text mechanism in topics.js: with a DOM/cookie mock it verifies applyMathAlts() hides the rendered <math> and shows the .math-alt twin exactly when the math-heavy tone is switched off.
nodes.languageNotes: Mocks document.cookie with a backing map so topics_pref round-trips, and keeps readyState 'loading' so init() side effects don't fire.

nodes.name: php_render_validator.py
nodes.summary: Selenium-based render validator: starts a PHP dev server, opens pages in headless Chrome, and fails on JS console errors (exit 1), unrendered $$ LaTeX (exit 2), or reading-column width overflow via the production layout_guardrail.js (exit 3).
nodes.languageNotes: Auto-restarts itself under `uv run`; --all-lessons discovers lessons by scanning for COURSE_METADATA blocks; check_width drives window.__layoutGuardrailCheck() on demand for deterministic CI.

nodes.name: check_unrendered_latex
nodes.summary: Runs in-page JS that finds $$…$$ blocks containing underscores or backslash commands that are not wrapped in a <div> (where markdown parsers mangle them) and outside math/code exclusions.

nodes.name: check_width
nodes.summary: Polls window.__layoutGuardrailCheck() until the reading column is measurable, then returns whether the page is ok, the allowed pixel width, and the offender list with details.

nodes.name: discover_lessons
nodes.summary: Finds lesson pages by scanning .php files' first 4 KB for a COURSE_METADATA block, distinguishing lessons from non-lesson PHP scripts.

nodes.name: php_validator.py
nodes.summary: Static validator for PHP lesson templates: runs php -l syntax checks, a string/comment-aware HTML tag-balance checker (after stripping PHP blocks, comments, script, and style), and checks for BOM/extra-close-tag/content-after-close issues.
nodes.languageNotes: strip_php_blocks tracks PHP string literals and comments so a ?> inside a string does not end the PHP block early; tag checks are skipped for pure-PHP logic files (functions.php, search*.php).

nodes.name: check_php_syntax
nodes.summary: Runs `php -l` on a file and returns (is_valid, message), handling missing PHP CLI and timeouts.

nodes.name: strip_php_blocks
nodes.summary: Removes <?php … ?> blocks while preserving newlines (for line numbers); string- and comment-aware so ?> inside PHP strings or comments is not treated as a real closing tag.

nodes.name: check_tag_balance
nodes.summary: Stack-based checker that opens/closes tracked HTML tags (void and self-closing elements excluded) over the stripped template, reporting unclosed, misnested, and unexpected closing tags with line numbers.

nodes.name: search_js_test.js
nodes.summary: Node smoke test for search.js internals (exposed via initSearch._internals): verifies detectMode regex/fuzzy/normal classification, smart-quote normalization, splitTerms, highlightText per mode, and extractMatchFromSnippet.

nodes.name: search_test.php
nodes.summary: PHP test suite for search_lib.php that builds temp-dir lesson fixtures and asserts the full search behavior: text normalization (umlauts, Greek, hyphens), regex/fuzzy/normal modes, snippet building, heading-slug URLs, caption ranking, citation author search, exclusions, and index cache invalidation.
nodes.languageNotes: Creates real fixture .php/.js files in sys_get_temp_dir() and cleans them up at the end; includes an mb_strpos end-of-block crash regression check.

nodes.name: topics_test.js
nodes.summary: Node smoke test for topics.js: verifies the TOPICS/CATEGORIES registries, cookie round-trip persistence, isEnabled/anyEnabled/isCatEnabled defaults, the 3-state scoreUnit() logic with reason strings, the layman lens, math-level clamping, CORE_PERSONAS, and the marked extension rendering [[t:topic]] blocks.
nodes.languageNotes: Mocks document.cookie with a backing map (including expiration deletion) and provides a functional marked mock that drives the real registered extension's start/tokenizer/renderer.

nodes.name: typo_checker.py
nodes.summary: Spell-checks prose inside PHP lesson templates: strips PHP/HTML/LaTeX/code, splits camelCase and hyphenated words, filters a whitelist plus a built-in ML/tech domain vocabulary, and reports misspellings with suggestions via pyspellchecker.
nodes.languageNotes: Whitelist lives next to the script (typo_whitelist.txt); a large TECH_DOMAIN_WORDS set (llm, softmax, vaswani, …) supplements the English dictionary to avoid flagging ML terminology.

nodes.name: strip_code_and_markup
nodes.summary: Removes pre/code/script/style blocks, comments, display+inline LaTeX, \cite-style macros, HTML tags, URLs, and markdown syntax so only human-readable prose remains (newlines preserved).

nodes.name: extract_words_with_lines
nodes.summary: Extracts (word, line) pairs from prose, skipping short words, splitting camelCase/PascalCase identifiers into sub-words, and splitting hyphenated and possessive words before checking.

nodes.name: check_file_typos
nodes.summary: Per-file pipeline: strip PHP, strip markup, extract words, drop whitelisted/domain words, run spell.unknown(), and build deduplicated issues with first-seen line, occurrence count, and suggestions.

nodes.name: typo_whitelist.txt
nodes.summary: One-word-per-line whitelist (~550 entries) suppressing typo_checker.py false positives: ML terminology (subword, neocognitron, rlhf), proper names (rumelhart, nietzsches), and informal forms (didn, aren).

nodes.name: typography_fix.html
nodes.summary: Headless regression test that loads production typography_fix.js over a synthetic .md column and asserts all-in-node conversion (both quote pairs, en-dash ranges, ellipsis) while <code> and .no-typo-fix content stay untouched.
nodes.languageNotes: Writes its verdict idempotently to <title> (TYPOGRAPHY_FIX PASS/FAIL) for the shell runner to grep; a 4s timeout guard fails on a stuck PENDING state.

nodes.name: typography_fix.sh
nodes.summary: Headless Chromium runner for typography_fix.html; dumps the DOM and greps the <title> for the PASS/FAIL verdict, skipping when chromium or the site is unreachable.

nodes.name: width_layout_guard.html
nodes.summary: Headless regression test for layout_guardrail.js over a synthetic 600px column: asserts wide normal elements are flagged while the same width inside .cl-block/.optional/.sideimage/.lg-scroll is exempt, and that __layoutGuardrailTag/__layoutGuardrailExclude work as expected.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs in three phases (baseline offenders, tag exemption, fresh-offender exclude) and reports a single idempotent verdict in <title>.

nodes.name: width_layout_guard.sh
nodes.summary: Headless Chromium runner for width_layout_guard.html; dumps the DOM with a virtual-time budget and greps the <title> for the PASS/FAIL verdict.

nodes.name: autofix.js
nodes.summary: CLI that reads the test runner's _stream.jsonl findings and auto-generates safe dark-mode CSS rules (font contrast fixes and optional stuck-white container fixes), inserting them into style.css after the dark-mode marker with a .bak-autofix backup, and writes autofix_report.json.
nodes.languageNotes: Aggregates per-page findings by selector|color key, generalizes selectors (strips dynamic IDs, drops bare tags), and only applies fixes that are not HUD/overlay or SVG/MathJax/Plotly elements; supports --dry-run and --only-critical.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point: validates stream/CSS paths, aggregates font issues and optional stuck-white clusters from _stream.jsonl, filters to safe fixes, renders the CSS block, inserts it into style.css at the dark-mode marker (with backup), and writes the report.

nodes.name: generalizeSelector
nodes.summary: Strips dynamic IDs and collapses duplicate classes from a CSS selector so many element-specific findings collapse into one rule; returns null for bare-tag selectors that are too broad to fix automatically.

nodes.name: groupByGeneralized
nodes.summary: Groups candidate fixes by their generalized selector, merging the affected pages and counting original element occurrences, and collects the bare-tag selectors that were skipped as needing manual fixes.

nodes.name: findDarkMarker
nodes.summary: Locates the insertion point in style.css: a /* ...darkmode... */ comment or the first html.dark rule, falling back to end-of-file, so generated rules land in the dark-mode section.

nodes.name: writeReport
nodes.summary: Writes autofix_report.json into the output dir, recording applied rules (selector, new/old color, severity, contrast, page list), stuck-white fixes, and the skipped unsafe fixes.

nodes.name: github-actions.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow ('Dark-mode check') triggered on pushes/PRs touching darkmode-ci/**, style.css, or PHP lessons: installs Chromium + php-cli, serves the blog on :8080, runs test.js with configurable wait/parallel/pages inputs, uploads screenshots, posts a PR summary comment, and exits non-zero when bugs are found.

nodes.name: bug-detector.js
nodes.summary: Detection core: matches light/dark element snapshots pairwise and flags theme-switch bugs (bg+color unchanged on a still-light dark background), WCAG AA font-readability violations, and stuck-white pixel clusters, skipping HUD, accents, backdrop, and math/plot elements.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports the shared constants DARK_PAGE_BG and the intentional indigo ACCENT_COLORS allowlist used to suppress false positives.

nodes.name: matchPairs
nodes.summary: Greedy nearest-neighbor matching of light and dark snapshot elements by identical selector within a 5px Manhattan distance, producing {light, dark} pairs for comparison.

nodes.name: detectThemeBugs
nodes.summary: Reports element pairs whose background and color barely changed between themes but whose dark background is still light (luminance > 0.7), with severity 'critical' (lum > 0.9) or 'warning', filtering out accents, HUD, backdrop, and tiny elements.

nodes.name: detectFontIssues
nodes.summary: Computes WCAG contrast of each text-bearing dark-mode element against its effective background (falling back to the dark page bg when transparent) and reports violations: severity critical (<2), bad (2-3), warn (3-4.5), or tiny-font (<11px text).

nodes.name: detectBlock
nodes.summary: Async orchestrator for one scroll block: runs matchPairs + detectThemeBugs + detectFontIssues on the snapshots and findStuckWhiteClusters on the two PNGs, returning {bugs, fontIssues, whiteClusters}.

nodes.name: color-utils.js
nodes.summary: Shared color math: parses rgb()/rgba() strings, computes WCAG 2.x relative luminance and contrast ratio, RGB distance, luminance bands, and picks a readable light foreground color against a dark background.

nodes.name: parseRgba
nodes.summary: Parses an rgb()/rgba() CSS color string into {r,g,b,a} (alpha defaults to 1), returning null on malformed input; the entry point for all color comparisons.

nodes.name: relLum
nodes.summary: Computes WCAG 2.x relative luminance from an {r,g,b} object using the sRGB linearization threshold (0.03928) and the 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 channel weights.

nodes.name: contrastRatio
nodes.summary: Computes the WCAG contrast ratio (Lmax+0.05)/(Lmin+0.05) between two parsed colors; the metric behind all font-readability thresholds.

nodes.name: pickReadableForeground
nodes.summary: Walks a list of safe light colors and returns the first whose contrast against the given dark background meets the minimum (default 4.5), used by autofix to choose replacement text colors.

nodes.name: element-snapshot.js
nodes.summary: Puppeteer page.evaluate helpers that capture every visible element's computed style (bg, color, font size, backdrop) and bounding rect as a flat snapshot, or identify the element under a given viewport point, with SVG/MathJax/Plotly tags skipped.
nodes.languageNotes: The skip-tag lists are re-inlined inside the page.evaluate closures because Node-side helpers are not visible in the browser context.

nodes.name: snapshotVisibleElements
nodes.summary: Captures up to maxElements (default 800) visible in-viewport elements as {sel, ancSel, bg, color, fontSize, hasText, backdrop, inlineBg/inlineColor, x,y,w,h} records built from getBoundingClientRect + getComputedStyle, skipping hidden, low-opacity, SVG, and math/plot nodes.

nodes.name: identifyElementAtPoint
nodes.summary: Uses document.elementsFromPoint to find the first meaningful element (skipping html/body/SVG) at viewport coordinates and returns its selector, colors, snippet of text, and positioning info — used to label stuck-white clusters.

nodes.name: pixel-diff.js
nodes.summary: PNG pixel-level comparison: builds difference masks between light and dark screenshots of the same block, then flood-fills them into bounding-box clusters to find stuck-white regions (white in both themes) and strongly changed regions.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles the pngjs 6.x vs 7.x sync-read API move by detecting PNG.PNG.sync once at load time.

nodes.name: findStuckWhiteClusters
nodes.summary: Masks pixels that are near-white (avg > whiteThreshold, default 235) in both light and dark screenshots with low color difference, then returns flood-filled clusters (default min 800 px, aspect-ratio capped) — the visual confirmation of theme-switch bugs.

nodes.name: findChangedClusters
nodes.summary: Masks pixels whose light/dark RGB sum-difference exceeds minDifference (default 100) and flood-fills them into clusters (default min 500 px), highlighting regions that did switch between themes.

nodes.name: floodClusters
nodes.summary: Iterative 4-neighborhood flood-fill over a binary mask collecting bounding boxes and pixel counts per cluster, filtering by minimum size, minimum extent, and maximum aspect ratio.

nodes.name: scroll-capture.js (lib)
nodes.summary: Generic Puppeteer scroll-and-screenshot library (ScrollCapture class): launches Chromium, opens isolated browser contexts, navigates with module-loader wait, scrolls in fixed steps with double-rAF settle, and captures screenshots + DOM snapshots per position in one or both themes.
nodes.languageNotes: Each page gets its own BrowserContext for cookie/storage isolation; scrollTo waits two requestAnimationFrame ticks to fix the pre-paint screenshot race.

nodes.name: ScrollCapture
nodes.summary: Core reusable capture engine: launch/close, openPage (isolated context), navigate (theme cookie + networkidle2 + _modulesLoaded wait), scrollTo (double-rAF), computeScrollPositions, captureAt (per-position, multi-theme, optional snapshot), and capturePage (full-page loop writing block-NN-yYYY-theme.png files).

nodes.name: scroll-capture.js (CLI)
nodes.summary: Thin CLI wrapper around lib/scroll-capture.js for one-off visual inspection: captures a page slug or URL in configurable themes/viewport/scroll steps, writing block PNGs and a scroll_capture.json metadata file.

nodes.name: selectors.js
nodes.summary: Selector classification for false-positive filtering: classifies elements as fixed HUD/overlay UI (drawer, search, topics overlays, toggles) by ancestor/id allowlists, and as skippable tags (SVG, canvas, MathJax/KaTeX, Plotly/ECharts); also builds tag+id+class CSS selectors.

nodes.name: isHudElement
nodes.summary: Returns true when a selector or its ancestor matches the FIXED_HUD_ANCESTORS class list or a FIXED_HUD_IDS id, so bug detection and autofix leave deliberate cross-theme UI (drawer, search, topic overlays) untouched.

nodes.name: isSkippableTag
nodes.summary: Returns true for selectors whose base tag is in the skip list (svg, canvas, br, script, ...) or which match MathJax/KaTeX/Plotly/ECharts patterns, since computed color on those elements is misleading.

nodes.name: theme-controller.js
nodes.summary: Puppeteer helpers that drive the blog's theme: toggle html.dark + write the theme cookie + update meta theme-color with a settle delay for MutationObservers, preset the cookie pre-navigation, and query the current theme.

nodes.name: setTheme
nodes.summary: Toggles the html.dark class in the page, writes the theme= light|dark cookie, updates the meta theme-color to #0f172a/#ffffff, and waits settleMs (default 1000) so observers and CSS transitions finish before the next screenshot.

nodes.name: presetCookie
nodes.summary: Sets the theme cookie at the browser level before navigating so a page boots directly in the desired theme instead of flashing the other one.

nodes.name: make-sxs.js
nodes.summary: Generates side-by-side comparison images (light | dark | dark-annotated with red boxes around stuck-white clusters read from _stream.jsonl) using ImageMagick +append, one per captured block per page, into the sxs/ directory.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for the darkmode-ci tool: declares pngjs and puppeteer-core dependencies and scripts (test, test:fast, test:single, test:json, capture, fix, fix:dry, fix:critical, fix:all) for the tester, capture CLI, and autofix variants.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Documentation for darkmode-ci: explains the three detection modes (theme-switch bugs, stuck-white clusters, WCAG font readability), CLI flags and env vars, autofix workflow, library API, output layout, exit codes, sample CI usage, and the detection-filtering notes (backdrops, indigo accents, img, math/plot, HUD).

nodes.name: test.js
nodes.summary: Main orchestrator CLI: for each of ~60 blog pages, scrolls in steps with a parallel browser-context worker pool, toggles light/dark per block, screenshots + snapshots, runs detectBlock, appends findings to _stream.jsonl, and writes bug_report.json / summary.json with an exit code for CI gating.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a fixed ALL_PAGES slug list of the full course; N async workers share one queue and one launched browser, and white-cluster centers are hit-tested via identifyElementAtPoint to attach element selectors.

nodes.name: testPage
nodes.summary: Per-page test loop: opens an isolated context, navigates, then for each scroll position captures light then dark (screenshot + DOM snapshot), runs detectBlock, hit-tests up to 5 white-cluster centers for element identification, and streams a JSONL record per block.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point: parses CLI/env options, launches ScrollCapture, fans the page queue out over `parallel` workers, writes partial.json incrementally plus final bug_report.json and summary.json, prints or emits JSON, and exits 1 when critical/bad font issues, theme bugs, or white clusters exist.

nodes.name: watch-and-fix.js
nodes.summary: Background watcher that polls _stream.jsonl every minute during a live test.js run and spawns `autofix.js --include-stuck-white` whenever the line count crosses a 10-block boundary or the run finishes, giving incremental CSS fixes while the long scan is still in progress.

nodes.name: test.html
nodes.summary: Self-contained 'Deep' adaptive-learning interface (test page): a single-page app that renders a root narrative full of inline 'portals' (\deep{}) that open into full-screen topic views via a vim-style open stack, with a force-directed knowledge graph, Temml LaTeX rendering, breadcrumb/visited-state tracking, and a light/dark theme.
nodes.languageNotes: Everything lives inline in one HTML file: a `Deep` IIFE module exposing register/relate/render/openTopic/goBack/toggleGraph plus getter-only topics/relations/openStack. Topic content uses custom macros (\rel{}, \deep{}, \latex{}, \latexblock{}) rewritten before Temml; \deep{} links register topics lazily and fetch their body from ./texts/<id>/. Some helpers (buildRelatedSection, bindRelatedItems, init) are defined twice in the file.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers a topic by id with a title and raw HTML content into the Deep topic store; the content is macro/LaTeX-processed and rendered into a full-screen view when the topic is opened.

nodes.name: relate
nodes.summary: Adds a typed relation (default 'related') between two topic ids into the relations list, deduplicated, which feeds both the related-topics section and the knowledge graph.

nodes.name: openTopic
nodes.summary: Core navigation: pushes a topic onto the vim-style open stack (popping back to it if already open), lazily loads content, builds/updates the full-screen .deep-view with a back button and related-topics section, then cross-fades between views and refreshes the breadcrumb.

nodes.name: goBack
nodes.summary: Pops the open stack, fades out the current view, re-activates the previous view (or root) and restores its saved scroll position, then updates the breadcrumb.

nodes.name: processContent
nodes.summary: Prepares topic HTML for display: rewrites \rel{from}{to}{type} macros into relations and \deep{id}{label} macros into clickable portal spans, then delegates \latexblock/\latex/$$/$ math to Temml.

nodes.name: renderGraph
nodes.summary: Renders topics/relations as a force-directed canvas graph (pairwise repulsion, edge attraction, center gravity) with hover highlighting, node dragging, and double-click-to-open, driven by requestAnimationFrame.

nodes.name: umwelt.html
nodes.summary: A-Frame 3D test scene (German) visualizing Uexküll's 'Umwelten': a beach with a jogging human, a following dog, and a flying butterfly, each wrapped in a translucent 'world bubble' with sensory particles, plus a dark AI scene of floating vector-space tokens — switching perceiver changes which world is visible.
nodes.languageNotes: Built from A-Frame primitives (no external models); grass/flowers/particles/AI tokens are generated in JS at load. Scene switching toggles entity visibility, a body CSS 'vision filter' (dog = desaturated), camera position, info-panel text, and WebAudio ambience (synth bird chirps + filtered noise waves).

nodes.name: switchScene
nodes.summary: Global scene switcher (human/dog/butterfly/ai): resets all world bubbles/particles/labels, reveals the active perceiver's bubble, sensory particles, and knowledge labels, swaps the info-panel text and body vision filter, repositions the camera, and retunes the WebAudio ambience.

nodes.name: tick
nodes.summary: requestAnimationFrame loop that animates the beach: the jogger walks and loops with swinging limbs, the dog chases with trotting legs, the butterfly flutters with flapping wings, world bubbles/particles follow their owners, AI data cubes bob, and the camera sways gently.

nodes.name: Steelman & Critique: Coherent Difference + World Models
nodes.summary: Long working critique of the two WIP chapters coherent_difference.php and coherent_world_models.php: it reconstructs each thesis, argues the strongest case by angle (S1-S8), then attacks that steelman from 13 angles (C1-C13) - vacuity of the never-fixed F/res/licence objects, the Tarski x indirect-realism collapse of the two-leg truth condition, and the self-reference problem - finishing with a scorecard and a prioritized list of fixes.

nodes.name: Formulary
nodes.summary: Course-wide math reference lesson (Part 6) collecting every generalized equation used across the textbook into grouped tables - numerical foundations, linear algebra, calculus/gradients, probability/statistics, NN building blocks, optimizers, and the Transformer - each with plain-English meaning, a full symbol definition, and its (however indirect) connection to LLMs.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure lesson template (include + Markdown tables inside <div class="md">); no PHP logic. Heavily uses LaTeX ($...$) for every equation and a symbol-collision note for overloaded symbols (sigma, T, L).

nodes.name: Model Theory: What a Model Is
nodes.summary: Part 4 lesson giving the exact mathematical discipline of model theory - first-order language/structure/theory, the theory-model Galois connection, Tarski's recursive satisfaction definition, the three pillars (completeness, compactness, downward Lowenheim-Skolem), nonstandard models and Skolem's paradox, and Morley's categoricity theorem - and tying each to the course's world-model and contact-point claims.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure lesson template (include + Markdown with LaTeX display math); uses <div class="optional md"> collapsible boxes and \cite macros. No PHP functions.

nodes.name: Recursion and the Shape of Coherent Difference
nodes.summary: Part 4 lesson locating recursion inside the sheaf-theoretic 'coherent difference' picture: the higher-coherence tower (infinity-sheaf / Cech nerve), the regress of licences, Spencer-Brown's distinction as a fixed point, Tarski's circle and the diagonal, the HoTT universe tower, proof-theoretic normalization as descent, confluence (Church-Rosser / Newman), and fixed-point theorems (Brouwer, Lawvere).
nodes.languageNotes: Pure lesson template (include + Markdown with LaTeX display math); uses <div class="optional md"> collapsibles and \cite / data-cite macros. No PHP functions.

nodes.name: The Model: One Object, Many Lenses
nodes.summary: Part 4 synthesis lesson unifying the course around a single claim: an LLM is simultaneously a physical system, a differentiable function, an information pipeline, a knowledge structure, a reasoning engine, and a potentially agentic system - describing each layer of description, the seams between them, and what the model is not (not a database, program, mind, or opaque black box).
nodes.languageNotes: Pure prose lesson template (include + Markdown); ends with an empty <div id="summary-container"> placeholder and has no companion JS module.

layers.name: Course Shell & Rendering Engine
layers.description: The PHP/JS/CSS infrastructure that serves, renders, navigates, searches, personalizes, and themes the textbook — including the course index, landing page, mobile plumbing, vendor styles, and embed/proxy utilities.

layers.name: Part 1 — Foundations
layers.description: The opening lessons on the history of AI and science, the history of language, and the numerical/linear-algebra/statistical/typo-theory bedrock (math I–IV, statistics I–II, geometry I–III).

layers.name: Part 2 — How Neural Networks Learn
layers.description: The learning mechanics: the smallest network, loss, derivatives and differentiation, backpropagation, automatic differentiation, activation functions, the optimizer, hyperparameters, live training, and reinforcement learning.

layers.name: Part 3 — Deep Learning & Vision
layers.description: Deep learning mechanics (deeplearning lab, ResNets/vanishing gradients, over/underfitting, layer norm, topology of representation) and the computer-vision stack (CNN, deconvolution, Inceptionism, ReLU folding).

layers.name: Part 4 — The Transformer Revolution
layers.description: Tokenization, embeddings, positional encoding, self-attention, the from-scratch trainable transformer with provenance/TDA/layer-summary tooling, and the surrounding theory (diffusion, algorithms, mechanistic interpretability, alternative architectures).

layers.name: Part 5 — Making AI Useful
layers.description: Practical LLM application: prompting, fine-tuning/post-training, RAG and semantic/web search, agents, reasoning, context windows, evaluation, inference/serving, training data and infrastructure, and reliability/safety.

layers.name: Part 6 — Bigger Questions

tour.title: Entry point: the course home and linear curriculum
tour.description: Start here: index.php is the landing page (hero + one interactive tile per course part) and index_full.php renders the entire curriculum in reading order by including every lesson module in sequence. Reading these two files together shows how a reader discovers and navigates the whole book, and where every lesson plugs in.
tour.languageLesson: No build step: index_full.php is a single PHP template that pulls lessons in via functions.php's incl("Human Title", "slug") helper — the linear course order is declared by hand, one line per lesson.

tour.title: The course shell: server-side infrastructure (functions.php)
tour.description: functions.php is the backbone every page depends on. It parses each lesson's <!-- COURSE_METADATA --> block to auto-build the drawer/index/progress, provides the js/css/incl asset loaders, the post-load JS orchestrator, and renders all the chrome (theme/topics/reader toggles, drawer, module nav, hero constellation). This is the single most important file for understanding how the shell is assembled.
tour.languageLesson: The drawer is generated by scanning lesson files: parse_course_metadata() reads each file's metadata comment, and render_module_nav()/get_module_nav_data() emit the prev/next data that start.js later wires up.

tour.title: Client runtime: markdown, citations, and bootstrapping
tour.description: helper.js renders each lesson's Markdown (protecting LaTeX and the index), processes \cite/\footcite macros against the bibliography, handles typography and lazy section init, and runs the global dark-mode observer. start.js is the site-wide bootstrap: Temml LaTeX rendering with a right-click source popup, dark mode, the mobile drawer, prev/next nav, the auto-glossary, and the loader checklist. Together they turn static .php prose into a living page.
tour.languageLesson: Lesson JS registers a loader in window.__moduleLoaderQueue; loader.js runs each loader concurrently (yielding once so the browser can paint) and ticks off a visible checklist — a dependency-free module system with no bundler.

tour.title: Design system and reading comfort
tour.description: style.css is the single global stylesheet: the --mn-* design tokens (cream-paper light palette with a full dark-mode override), self-hosted fonts, and every component style from the course shell down to Tufte sidenotes, aurora clusters, and the ~1,000 dark-mode rescue rules. polish.js and typography_fix.js layer on the reading comfort — anchors, scroll-spy, copy buttons, citation previews, and silent typographic autocorrect.
tour.languageLesson: Theming is pure CSS custom properties: start.js toggles html.dark and a MutationObserver in helper.js re-renders charts — no per-theme JS, just a token swap plus a watcher.

tour.title: Personalization, progress, and search
tour.description: topics.js is the personalization engine (window.BlogTopics): a topic picker, a math-comfort slider, audience presets, and per-lesson 'learned' tracking that tuck/dim/reveal in-lesson sections and home tiles. progress_tracker.js paints the segmented 'where I've been' bar, and the search trio (search.php endpoint, search_lib.php indexer, search.js overlay) gives Ctrl/Cmd+K full-text search with normal/regex/fuzzy modes.
tour.languageLesson: Persistence is dual: state lives in localStorage and is mirrored to a size-guarded cookie (topics_pref) so it survives the static-file deployment; the cookie write is skipped once near 4 KB.

tour.title: Part 1 — Foundations: the bedrock lessons
tour.description: The book opens with history and math. history.php + history.js trace the convergence of counting tools, number systems, logic, and computation into AI (with an OR/XOR separability demo), and language.php + language.php's timeline run language from Sanskrit to LLMs. Then the four math chapters lay the groundwork: numerical foundations (math_i), linear algebra (math_ii), high-dimensional geometry and type theory (math_iii + math_iii_hott.js), and affine maps & the ReLU fold (math_iv + math_iv_affine.js).
tour.languageLesson: Lessons interleave inline JS: math_iv_affine.js keeps a DOM-free pure-math core (matrices, folds, Hopf tubes) separate from its five canvas labs, and guards the shared math pipeline with an IntersectionObserver-based lazy init.

tour.title: Part 1 — The geometry and statistics trilogy
tour.description: Foundations finish with three deep 'working mathematics' chapters that tie each mathematical object to the layer that uses it. geometry_i.php is a history of geometry (shells to Riemannian manifolds); geometry_ii.php is the geometric toolkit behind networks (inner product, SVD, convolution, symmetry); geometry_iii.php is working algebraic topology (homology, homotopy, persistent homology). statistics_i/ii.php + statistics.js add probability, inference, entropy, and the LLM probability labs.
tour.languageLesson: statistics.js is a single shared lab re-bootstrapped by thin loaders (statistics_i.js / statistics_ii.js guarded by window.__statisticsModuleLoaded), so the same ~20 Plotly labs run standalone or inside the combined course page.

tour.title: Part 2 — How Neural Networks Learn
tour.description: The learning mechanics, in reading order: the smallest network (minimalneuron), why non-linearity is needed (activationlab), what loss is (losslab), the derivative as a steepness check (derivativelab), and differentiation (differentiation). This is the conceptual spine that makes backprop and automatic differentiation land.
tour.languageLesson: Every lab is a self-contained module exposing one global namespace (e.g. a 'LossLab' object) plus a load…Module() entry point; TF.js is used for the live-training demos, Plotly for the static plots.

tour.title: Part 2 — Backprop, autodiff, optimization & live training
tour.description: The payoff of Part 2: backproplab.js animates a forward/backward pass through a 3-4-4-2 net with hoverable cones of influence; autodiff.js builds a tape-based reverse-mode engine and a gradient-landscape animator; optimizerlab.js races SGD/Momentum/Adam; and traininglab.js/trainiglab.php train a live XOR network with decision boundaries and weight heatmaps. reinforcement_learning.php closes with the math of RL and RLHF/DPO.
tour.languageLesson: backproplab.js renders the network as SVG with animated forward/backward pulses and derives per-neuron equations with LaTeX underbraces on click — the same 'make the math touchable' philosophy as the rest of the book.

tour.title: Part 3 — Deep Learning & Vision
tour.description: Deep-learning mechanics first: deeplearninglab (single neuron to deep nets, UAP, residual connections), resnetlab (vanishing gradients vs the residual superhighway), overandunderfittinglab (bias-variance and the extrapolation/hallucination metaphor), normalizationlab (Layer/Group Norm), and topology (homeomorphisms bound a network's power). Then the vision stack: computer_vision.js runs live TF.js convolutions over a stop sign, with deconvolution, inceptionism, and origami's ReLU-folding picture.
tour.languageLesson: computer_vision.js runs real convolutions through TF.js and computes the per-pixel convolution math on hover, while origami.js folds the data manifold in 1-D/3-D to show how ReLU stacks manufacture linear separability.

tour.title: Part 4 — The Transformer Revolution
tour.description: The flagship part. The from-scratch trainable transformer (transformer.php + transformer.js) assembles tokenization, embeddings, positional encoding, attention, FFN, unembedding, loss, and optimizer into one machine — instrumented by provenance.js (hover any number to see its computation), tda_live.js (live topological TDA), and transformer_layer_summary.js (what each layer is doing). The supporting lessons walk the pieces: tokenization, embeddings, positional encoding, attention, diffusion, algorithms, and mechanistic interpretability.
tour.languageLesson: transformer.js implements a full decoder-only Transformer in the browser (causal multi-head attention, pre-LN, GELU, sinusoidal PE) and trains it with TensorFlow.js; provenance.js hooks onForward to build a value-matched registry so every rendered number is hoverable.

tour.title: Part 5 — Making AI Useful
tour.description: Practical LLM application: promptengineering, finetuninglab (SFT → DPO/GRPO → RLHF), reasoning & test-time compute, contextwindows ('lost in the middle'), the retrieval stack (rag, vectorsearch, websearch), agents, and the reliability/serving concerns (hallucinations, reliability, inference_optimization, production_serving). These are the chapters that turn a trained model into a product.
tour.languageLesson: The retrieval lessons (rag.js, vectorsearch.js, websearch.js) each ship an interactive pipeline diagram plus a tiny in-browser search that scores documents with a BM25-like keyword score and tag-based cosine similarity — the same search machinery used by the site's own search_lib.php.

tour.title: Part 6 — Bigger Questions & the closing arc
tour.description: The book closes on the ecosystem and frontier: the global AI ecosystem, the untold history, the mind that built machines, the wider world of models beyond LLMs, deep theory, frontier topics, alignment, law, philosophy, unexpected capabilities, AI-for-science, existential risk, myths, software, and the interactive appendix. These set the technical content in its historical, social, and ethical frame.

tour.title: Supporting subsystems: demos, Python references, Coq, and QA
tour.description: Finally, the machinery behind the book. lndw/ is a standalone 'Wie funktionieren LLMs?' presentation deck (presentation.js engine + intuition/embedding/attention slides + sheaves/HoTT decks) that previews the same interactive visualizations. py/ mirrors the in-browser lessons in runnable Python (autodiff, minimal-neuron XOR, vision classifiers). coq/coherent_world_models/ is the 19-file Coq formalization of the 'Coherent World Models' chapter. And the tests/ + darkmode-ci/ suites are what keep it all correct: PHP/JS/link/typo/LaTeX validators, headless layout guards, and the Puppeteer dark-mode screenshot CI.
tour.languageLesson: The QA layer is a no-framework test battery: php_validator.py strips PHP/comments then stack-checks HTML tags; js_validator.py is a hand-rolled tokenizer + regex lint; and darkmode-ci's test.js scrolls each page, toggles html.dark, screenshots, and lets autofix.js write safe CSS back into style.css.
